articles.body: Tom Waits' rare 'Orphans: Bonus' EP, previously available only on vinyl, is now streaming. The release gives a wider audience access to a collection that has been a collectors' item since it first appeared, and it is the latest in a run of catalogue moves that have brought Waits' rarities to streaming. Waits, one of the most distinctive voices in American music, has always had a complicated relationship with the digital era, and the arrival of the EP on streaming is a small event for his fans. The 'Orphans' material dates from the mid-2000s sessions that produced one of his most sprawling projects, and the bonus EP has been sought after by collectors ever since. For longtime listeners, the streaming release is a chance to hear the songs without tracking down a vinyl copy. For new listeners, it is an entry point to a catalogue that rewards digging. The release is a reminder that even in the streaming age, some music still takes its time to arrive.

articles.title: Blackpink's Jisoo debuts buoyant single 'Sun Showers'
articles.description: Blackpink's Jisoo has debuted a buoyant new single, 'Sun Showers,' in her latest solo move. The release continues the solo run from Blackpink's members, who have each built individual careers alongside the group's work, and it arrives as K-pop's solo stars dominate the charts.
articles.body: Blackpink's Jisoo has debuted a buoyant new single, 'Sun Showers,' in her latest solo move. The release continues the solo run from Blackpink's members, who have each built individual careers alongside the group's work, and it arrives as K-pop's solo stars dominate the charts — including on Billboard's World Albums chart this week, where K-pop acts swept the top spots. Jisoo's single is described as buoyant, a bright pop turn that plays to her strengths as a vocalist and a star. The solo careers of Blackpink's four members have become one of the defining stories of pop in the last two years, with each finding a distinct lane. For Jisoo, 'Sun Showers' is the latest step in that journey, and it comes as the group's own future remains a subject of constant speculation. For fans, the single is a welcome new release from an artist whose solo work has been eagerly awaited. The song is out now on streaming.

articles.title: K-pop sweeps Billboard's World Albums chart, led by P1Harmony's 'BLOW UP' at No. 1
articles.description: K-pop acts have swept the top spots on Billboard's World Albums chart for the week ending November 21, led by P1Harmony's new mini album 'BLOW UP' at No. 1 — the group's first No. 1 on the chart, alongside their first No. 1 on the Top Album Sales chart. ILLIT's 'BREAK EVEN' held at No. 2 in its third week, Stray Kids placed four albums on the chart, and BTS landed three, with 'Proof' re-entering at No. 10 in its 226th week.
articles.body: K-pop acts have swept the top spots on Billboard's World Albums chart for the week ending November 21, led by P1Harmony's new mini album 'BLOW UP' at No. 1 — the group's first No. 1 on the chart, alongside their first No. 1 on the Top Album Sales chart. 'BLOW UP' also tied P1Harmony's best-ever rank on the Billboard 200, debuting at No. 4. ILLIT's latest mini album 'BREAK EVEN' stayed strong at No. 2 in its third week on the World Albums chart, and it also became the group's first album ever to spend more than one week on the Billboard 200. Stray Kids once again charted four albums on the week's World Albums chart, with 'THIS & THAT' at No. 3 in its 14th week and 'KARMA' at No. 7 in its 61st. CORTIS's 'GREENGREEN' held at No. 4 in its 28th week, ENHYPEN's 'THE SIN : BLISS' at No. 5, and xikers' new 'ROUTE ZERO : The CALLING' debuted at No. 6. BTS landed three albums on the chart: 'Proof' re-entered at No. 10 in its 226th week, with 'Map of the Soul: 7 ~The Journey~' at No. 12 and 'Love Yourself: Answer' at No. 17 in its 208th week. League of Legends' virtual group K/DA, NewJeans, BOYNEXTDOOR, ATEEZ and LE SSERAFIM rounded out the top 25 — a chart that reads as a map of K-pop's global reach.

articles.title: Air-raid sirens sound in Kaliningrad region for the first time since the full-scale war began
articles.description: Air-raid sirens sounded in Russia's Kaliningrad region on the evening of November 21, reportedly for the first time since the start of the full-scale war. Governor Alexei Besprozvannykh said the drone-danger alert system went off in the Neman district on the Lithuanian border after a 'suspicious object from Lithuania' was detected. The alert followed a Ukrainian drone attack on the cargo ship Sparta II in the Gulf of Finland earlier the same day.
articles.body: On the evening of November 21, air-raid sirens sounded across parts of Russia's Kaliningrad region, and according to media reports it was the first time this had happened since the start of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Kaliningrad governor Alexei Besprozvannykh said the drone-danger warning system was triggered in the Neman district, on the border with Lithuania, after it detected what he called a 'suspicious object from Lithuania'. Local residents also reported drone flyovers in the port city of Baltiysk, home to Russia's Baltic Fleet. The alert came hours after Ukrainian drones attacked the cargo ship Sparta II in the Gulf of Finland; the vessel, which sails between Leningrad region and Kaliningrad, caught fire and its crew was evacuated, though Russian officials said it would continue on to Kaliningrad. Lithuania's foreign minister firmly denied that Lithuanian airspace had been used for any attack on Kaliningrad or other Russian targets. The episode matters because it brings the war's air-raid reality to a Russian exclave that had been untouched by sirens for nearly five years, and it adds a new flashpoint between Russia and its NATO neighbours on the Baltic.

articles.title: Trump again calls Putin 'my friend' — and mixes up the Yalta and Tehran conferences
articles.description: In a new development, Donald Trump posted a series of images on Truth Social about his recent meeting with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, captioning a photo with Putin 'My friend'. The BBC's Russian service noticed that a photo of Stalin, Churchill and Roosevelt in the post was taken at the 1943 Tehran conference, not the 1945 Yalta conference Trump appeared to have in mind. Trump had already called Putin a friend during the Shenzhen meeting itself on November 19.
articles.body: US President Donald Trump has again publicly called Vladimir Putin a friend, this time in a Truth Social post published overnight on November 22, in a new development on a story already covered earlier this week. The post featured a series of images devoted to his recent meeting with the leaders of China and Russia, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, in Shenzhen, including one photograph of Trump with Putin captioned 'My friend'. As the BBC's Russian service pointed out, another image in the post — a famous photograph of Stalin, Churchill and Roosevelt — was taken in 1943 at the Tehran conference, not in 1945 at Yalta, which Trump apparently had in mind when drawing a parallel with the three-way summit. Trump had already called Putin a friend in person during the Shenzhen talks. On November 19, Trump, Putin and Xi held trilateral talks on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen — the first meeting of the three leaders in this format — and media compared it to the 1945 Yalta conference, where the leaders of the USSR, Britain and the US carved up spheres of influence in Europe. The final declaration from Shenzhen was widely described as empty, and no breakthrough on Ukraine emerged. The new post matters because it shows Trump doubling down on his warm personal framing of Putin even as he pushes for a Ukraine peace deal, and the historical mix-up has become a talking point in its own right.

articles.title: Denmark urges EU states to stop issuing tourist visas to Russians
articles.description: Denmark has proposed that EU countries stop issuing tourist visas to Russians and stop recognising Russian non-biometric passports, two diplomats told Reuters. Copenhagen sent a note with the proposals to EU governments and will present them at an ambassadors' meeting in Brussels on November 23. The move follows the arrest of two Danish citizens accused of plotting to assassinate Ukrainian rapper Kyivstoner on orders from Russian intelligence.
articles.body: Denmark has called on European Union countries to introduce further restrictions on Russians entering the Schengen area, in a new development following Copenhagen's expulsion of Russia's military attaché earlier this week. According to two diplomats cited by Reuters, Denmark circulated a note to EU governments proposing an end to the issuance of tourist visas to Russian citizens, and a refusal to recognise Russian non-biometric passports — the old-style foreign travel documents. Copenhagen is due to present the proposals at a meeting of EU ambassadors in Brussels on November 23. The push comes after Danish police arrested two Danish citizens on charges of preparing an assassination attempt against Ukrainian rapper Kyivstoner (Albert Vasiliev) during his trip to Denmark in September, allegedly on orders from Russian intelligence services. Denmark has already announced it will expel the Russian military attaché, who must leave within seven days, and will sharply curtail visa issuance to Russians. The European Commission is already discussing visa restrictions for Russians as part of a 22nd sanctions package against Russia. If adopted, the measures would tighten one of the last relatively open travel routes for ordinary Russians into Europe and deepen the diplomatic fallout from the alleged assassination plot.

articles.title: Wildberries founder Tatyana Kim steps down as CEO after EU sanctions
articles.description: Tatyana Kim has left her post as CEO of Wildberries, Russia's largest online marketplace, after the European Union imposed sanctions on her. The role has been taken by top manager Alexei Kulikov, according to Russia's corporate registry. The departure marks a rare shake-up at the top of one of Russia's biggest e-commerce companies.
articles.body: Tatyana Kim has stepped down as chief executive of Wildberries, Russia's largest online marketplace, days after the European Union imposed sanctions against her. According to data from Russia's Unified State Register of Legal Entities, the post has been taken by senior company manager Alexei Kulikov. Kim founded Wildberries in 2004 and built it into Russia's dominant e-commerce platform, becoming one of the country's richest women in the process. The company has faced a turbulent period, including a deadly 2024 office shooting linked to a corporate dispute and a merger with the Russ outdoor-advertising group that created the combined RWB holding. The EU sanctions against Kim are part of the bloc's latest pressure measures on prominent Russian business figures. Her departure matters because Wildberries is a backbone of Russian online retail, used by millions of shoppers and hundreds of thousands of small sellers, and a change at the top — forced by sanctions rather than business reasons — signals how Western restrictions are now reaching deep into Russia's consumer economy.

articles.title: German intelligence officers are questioning some Russians after passport control at airports
articles.description: Since at least early September 2026, German intelligence officers have been asking some Russian citizens to answer questions after they clear passport control at German airports. Meduza reports on who is conducting the interviews and why, as Germany tightens scrutiny of Russian travellers amid espionage and sabotage fears. The practice adds another layer of friction for Russians travelling to the EU.
articles.body: Since at least early September 2026, German intelligence officers have been approaching some Russian citizens for interviews after they pass through passport control at German airports, Meduza reports. The conversations take place once travellers have formally cleared border checks, and those targeted are asked to answer questions — the report examines who exactly is conducting them and what the authorities are trying to learn. The practice comes against a backdrop of heightened German concern about Russian espionage, sabotage and influence operations in Europe, following a series of suspected Russian-linked incidents including arson, cyberattacks and the alleged assassination plot in Denmark. Germany has been among the countries pushing for tighter handling of Russian nationals, and the airport interviews appear to be part of a broader intelligence effort to map networks and intentions among travellers from Russia. For ordinary Russian visitors the development matters because it adds an unpredictable, potentially lengthy step to entering Germany even after a visa has been granted, and it reflects how routine travel from Russia is increasingly treated as a security matter across the EU.

articles.title: Ukraine clause was dropped from the Trump–Putin–Xi 'peace declaration' at Washington's request, Finland's president says
articles.description: A provision on Ukraine was removed from the 'peace declaration' issued after the Trump–Putin–Xi meeting in Shenzhen at Washington's request, Finnish President Alexander Stubb has said. The declaration instead called on the International Criminal Court not to 'abuse its powers' and proposed reforming the UN. The disclosure adds to doubts about whether the Shenzhen summit produced anything of substance for Ukraine.
articles.body: A provision on Ukraine was dropped from the so-called 'peace declaration' issued by Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping after their trilateral meeting in Shenzhen — and it was removed at Washington's request, according to Finnish President Alexander Stubb. The declaration that was eventually published contained no meaningful language on Ukraine; instead, the three leaders called on the International Criminal Court not to 'abuse its powers' and proposed reforming the United Nations. The revelation is significant because the Shenzhen meeting on November 19 — the first time the three leaders had met in this format — was billed in some quarters as a potential 'new Yalta', a grand bargain on the post-war order. Instead, analysts concluded that China emerged as the main winner, the final declaration was largely empty, and nothing concrete was agreed on ending Russia's war in Ukraine. Stubb's account suggests the US itself asked for the Ukraine language to be taken out, which raises fresh questions about how far Washington is willing to go in pressing Moscow on the war — and about what, if anything, the much-hyped summit actually delivered.

articles.title: Russia's deputy PM says Crimean Bridge arch and main girder are damaged and repair timeline is unclear
articles.description: Russia's deputy prime minister has said the arch and main girder of the Crimean Bridge were damaged in Ukraine's latest strike, and it is unclear how long repairs will take. The admission is the most detailed Russian acknowledgement yet of the damage to the strategic crossing. It follows Ukraine's repeated attacks on the bridge, which links the annexed peninsula to mainland Russia.
articles.body: Russia's deputy prime minister has acknowledged that the arch and the main girder of the Crimean Bridge were damaged in Ukraine's latest strike, and that the timeline for repairs is unclear — the most detailed official Russian admission of the damage so far. The bridge, which links the Russian-annexed Crimean peninsula to Russia's Krasnodar region across the Kerch Strait, has been repeatedly targeted by Ukrainian strikes since the start of the full-scale war, and has been hit several times before. The damage to the arch and main girder is significant because these are load-bearing elements of the structure, and repairs to them would take far longer than patching a road deck. Ukrainian officials have argued the bridge cannot survive the war in its current form, while President Zelenskyy has said the crossing 'will not stand'. The bridge is a vital military supply route for Russian forces in southern Ukraine as well as a potent symbol of the annexation, which is why it remains one of Kyiv's highest-value targets. The Russian admission matters because it confirms the strike achieved structural — not merely cosmetic — damage, and it comes as Moscow has refused to discuss a ceasefire following the attacks on the bridge.

articles.title: Drone strike destroys apartment block entrance in Dymer near Kyiv; one body recovered, more than 10 people unaccounted for
articles.description: A Russian drone strike destroyed an entire entrance of a five-storey apartment building in the village of Dymer, near Kyiv, overnight on November 21–22. Rescue workers recovered one body from the rubble, and more than 10 people were still unaccounted for as of Sunday morning. The strike was part of a mass overnight drone attack on Ukraine involving 186 drones.
articles.body: A Russian drone strike overnight on November 21–22 destroyed an entire entrance of a five-storey apartment building in the village of Dymer, in the Kyiv region, leaving rescuers searching the rubble for survivors. Ukraine's State Emergency Service said one body had been recovered from under the debris by Sunday morning, while more than 10 people were still unaccounted for and could be trapped beneath the collapsed structure. Photographs from the scene showed the stairwell section of the building completely destroyed. The strike on Dymer was part of a large overnight attack in which Russia launched 186 attack drones at Ukraine, 72 of them jet-powered, with hits recorded at 18 locations. Air defences shot down or suppressed 161 of the drones. The attack also damaged a business in Lozova in the Kharkiv region and hit targets in Zaporizhzhia, where three people were injured. The Dymer strike is a stark reminder that even as diplomatic talk of ceasefires continues, Russia's nightly drone campaign keeps hitting civilian housing far from the front line, and the casualty count in Dymer may still rise as rescue work continues.

articles.title: Russia attacks Ukraine with 186 drones overnight; air defences down 161, hits recorded in 18 locations
articles.description: Russia launched 186 attack drones at Ukraine overnight on November 21–22, 72 of them jet-powered, Ukraine's air force said. Air defences shot down or suppressed 161 drones, but hits were recorded at 18 locations. A residential building was destroyed in Dymer near Kyiv, and three people were injured in Zaporizhzhia.
articles.body: Russian forces launched a mass drone attack on Ukraine overnight on November 21–22, firing 186 attack drones, including 72 jet-powered ones, according to Ukraine's air force. The attack began at 6pm on November 21 and continued through the night. As of 8am on Sunday, air defences had shot down or suppressed 161 of the drones, but strikes were recorded at 18 locations across the country. The heaviest damage was in the village of Dymer in the Kyiv region, where a drone destroyed an entire entrance of a five-storey apartment building; one body was recovered and more than 10 people were unaccounted for. In Zaporizhzhia, three people were injured in strikes on the city, and a business caught fire in Lozova in the Kharkiv region after a hit. The attack fits the pattern of Russia's nightly drone campaign, which has intensified sharply: over the past week Russia fired around 2,700 drones, nearly 1,460 guided aerial bombs and 165 missiles at 20 Ukrainian regions. The scale of the overnight attack shows that, despite diplomatic talk of a possible ceasefire, Russia's air campaign against Ukrainian cities and infrastructure is continuing at full intensity.

articles.title: Odesa schools switch to remote learning for a week after blackout; power, water and heating disrupted
articles.description: All schools in Odesa will teach remotely from November 23 to 27 after Russian strikes knocked out power, water and heating across the city. Trams and trolleybuses have stopped running, replaced by buses on some routes. The blackout that began on the evening of November 21 was still continuing on Sunday morning — a new development in the Odesa power crisis.
articles.body: All schools in Odesa will switch to remote learning from November 23 to 27 inclusive, the city council's education department announced, in a new development in the city's blackout crisis. The decision was taken because of severe disruptions to heating, electricity and water after Russian attacks badly damaged Odesa's main power networks. Kindergartens will operate only with duty groups for children of critical-infrastructure workers. Teachers have prepared recorded video lessons for pupils who cannot join live classes because of outages, and parents are urged to charge phones, tablets and laptops whenever power returns — devices can also be charged at 'invincibility points' set up in schools. The blackout began on the evening of November 21, when most of the city lost power and all electric public transport stopped; replacement buses are running on some routes at 25 hryvnias a ride. By the morning of November 22, energy workers had managed to partially restore power to critical infrastructure, but the grid in Odesa and surrounding districts remains in an extremely difficult state, according to DTEK and Ukrenergo. The situation follows a Russian strike on a DTEK energy facility on the morning of November 20 that left 41,000 families without power. The week of remote schooling shows how strikes on energy infrastructure are now disrupting everyday civilian life — education, transport, heating and water — across a major Ukrainian city.

articles.title: Zelenskyy: NATO membership remains on the table and is Ukraine's clearest security guarantee
articles.description: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Ukraine's NATO membership remains under discussion with allies and the United States, with no decision yet, and that it depends on how the war ends. He called membership Ukraine's most important security guarantee and said it would also strengthen NATO. He added that outside the alliance, Ukraine's roughly million-strong army would need its own missiles, artillery, aircraft and air defences.
articles.body: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says the question of Ukraine's NATO membership remains on the agenda in talks with allies and the United States, with no specific decision made yet and the outcome depending on when and how the war ends. Speaking after a meeting of the Coalition of the Willing, Zelenskyy said the issue had been raised by France and other allies, and he described NATO membership as Ukraine's most important security guarantee. He argued membership would benefit both sides: Ukraine's army, its experience and its military technology would strengthen the alliance, while for Ukraine it would be the less costly option — outside NATO, he said, an army of around a million soldiers would need its own missiles, artillery, aviation and the ability to defend its airspace independently. Zelenskyy also confirmed that the US side had previously asked in negotiations whether Ukraine would be prepared to withdraw its troops from the part of Donbas still under Ukrainian control in exchange for NATO membership. His comments came as the shape of post-war security guarantees is being hotly debated: Trump's envoy Jared Kushner has claimed Russia is 'satisfied' with Article 5-style guarantees for Ukraine, while Zelenskyy has said he is not sure Kyiv and Washington understand those guarantees the same way, and Russia's deputy foreign minister Sergei Ryabkov has called NATO-style guarantees unacceptable. For Zelenskyy, keeping formal NATO membership on the table matters because it is the guarantee he considers the most credible — and the hardest for Moscow to accept.

articles.title: EU budget draft keeps up to €100 billion for Ukraine in 2028–2034 despite overall cuts
articles.description: European Council President António Costa has presented a draft EU budget for 2028–2034 of about €1.78 trillion — 10% smaller than the European Commission's proposal — while preserving up to €100 billion for Ukraine through a dedicated Ukraine Reserve. EU leaders will discuss the plan in Brussels on November 26–27. The funding would sit above the budget's spending ceilings.
articles.body: European Council President António Costa presented his proposal for the EU's long-term budget for 2028–2034 on November 21, and despite cutting overall spending by €204 billion — about 10% below the European Commission's initial plan — it preserves up to €100 billion for Ukraine. The total budget would be around €1.78 trillion in current prices. Support for Ukraine would come through a dedicated instrument, the Ukraine Reserve, worth up to €100 billion in current prices, or €88.869 billion in constant 2025 prices — matching the Commission's original proposal. The funding would sit above the multi-year budget's spending ceilings and could take the form of budget guarantees, non-repayable grants and loans backed by the EU budget, with additional subsidies possible to cover Ukraine's borrowing costs; humanitarian needs could be funded through the EU's external assistance tools. Costa said the cuts were needed to keep national contributions at a reasonable level. The proposal is not yet final: EU leaders are due to discuss it at a European Council meeting in Brussels on November 26–27, and the whole budget must eventually be approved unanimously by all 27 member states with the European Parliament's consent. The news matters for Kyiv because it signals that long-term European financial backing is holding even as budgets tighten — and the EU is separately trying to persuade Canada and the UK to increase their support to help cover a projected €70 billion Ukrainian funding gap in 2027.

articles.title: Ukraine and the UK agree joint production of long-range strike drones
articles.description: Ukraine and the United Kingdom have signed project agreements to jointly produce Ukrainian long-range strike drones in Britain. The UK will provide financing, and the drones will be delivered to Ukraine's Defence Forces. No numbers or production start dates were disclosed, but the deal deepens the two countries' defence-industrial partnership.
articles.body: Ukraine and the United Kingdom have agreed to launch joint production of Ukrainian long-range strike drones, with the drones to be manufactured in Britain for Ukraine's Defence Forces. Defence ministers Yevhenii Khmara of Ukraine and Wes Streeting of the UK signed the project agreements, Ukraine's defence ministry announced. Under the deal, the British side will provide financing for production, while the jointly produced medium- and long-range strike drones will be handed over to the Ukrainian military. The announcement did not specify how many drones would be built or when production would begin. The agreement builds on an already close UK–Ukraine defence relationship — Britain has been one of Kyiv's largest military supporters — and it reflects a broader shift toward co-production rather than simple arms donations, giving Ukraine a more sustainable supply of the long-range weapons it uses to strike military targets deep inside Russia. It also fits the pattern of Ukraine's drone industry expanding abroad as domestic production scales up: Kyiv now produces more military drones than all NATO countries combined, according to recent reports. For Ukraine, British-built versions of its own proven drone designs could ease pressure on domestic factories that are themselves targets of Russian strikes.

articles.title: Melania Trump says ceasefire talks are under way and a deal could come before Christmas; Trump working on a larger truce
articles.description: First Lady Melania Trump says she is in talks with both Kyiv and Moscow and hopes a new ceasefire can be reached before Christmas, building on the Oleshky humanitarian evacuation she helped broker. President Trump said Washington is now working on a larger version of that local truce. The comments come as the US pushes for a broader peace deal, but no terms or timeline have been confirmed.
articles.body: First Lady Melania Trump has said she is holding talks with representatives of both Ukraine and Russia and hopes a new ceasefire agreement can be reached before Christmas. Speaking at the All-American Christmas Tree Lighting event and in a Fox News interview, she said she dreams above all of more ceasefire agreements, adding that a deal could be reached 'quite quickly' if Ukraine and Russia show willingness, and that negotiations are already under way. Her remarks build on the humanitarian operation she helped broker in late October in the occupied town of Oleshky, in the Kherson region, where a local ceasefire from October 27 to November 1 allowed the evacuation of around 800 civilians and the delivery of food, water, medicine and generator fuel. President Donald Trump, also speaking to Fox News, praised the Oleshky operation as 'wonderful' and said Washington is now 'working on a larger version of this' — a bigger truce modelled on the same humanitarian template. Ukraine has said it plans further humanitarian missions to occupied areas of the Kherson region, which would require new security arrangements. The first lady has also been involved in the issue of Ukrainian children taken to Russia, appointing a representative, Mark Beckman, to keep communication open with both sides, and she was recently awarded Ukraine's Order of Princess Olga. Whether the Christmas timeline is realistic remains unclear: no terms have been published, Russia has refused ceasefire talks after the Crimean Bridge strikes, and fighting — including the overnight drone attacks — continues at full intensity.

articles.title: 131 clashes on the front in a day; Russia fired about 2,700 drones, 1,460 glide bombs and 165 missiles at Ukraine in a week
articles.description: Ukraine's General Staff reported 131 combat engagements on the front over the past day, with the Pokrovsk direction among the most active, and said Ukrainian forces neutralised 2,310 Russian soldiers. Over the past week Russia fired around 2,700 drones, nearly 1,460 guided aerial bombs and 165 missiles at 20 Ukrainian regions. Russian troops also advanced near Dobropillia, capturing three settlements south of the town.
articles.body: Ukrainian forces repelled or held 131 combat engagements along the front over the past day, Ukraine's General Staff reported, with the Pokrovsk direction remaining one of the most active sectors. Ukrainian officials said 2,310 Russian soldiers were neutralised over the same period. The figures cap a week of intense Russian air attacks: over the past seven days Russia launched around 2,700 drones, nearly 1,460 guided aerial bombs and 165 missiles against 20 Ukrainian regions, hitting energy infrastructure, railways and civilian areas. On the ground, Russian troops advanced near Dobropillia, capturing the settlements of Bilitske, Matyasheve and Svitlo to the south of the town and approaching it from the south and south-east, according to Ukrainian military analyst Kostiantyn Mashovets. Ukrainian monitoring group Deep State also reported Russian advances near Kostiantynivka and Kramatorsk. At the same time, Ukrainian forces reported a breakthrough into Russia's Kursk region, taking the village of Novyi Put, and a covert counter-offensive operation in the Kharkiv region that disrupted Russian encirclement plans. The weekly bombardment figures underline the scale of the air war Ukraine is absorbing even as the front line grinds on: the strikes are aimed systematically at the energy grid as winter sets in, with five regions reporting power cuts after the latest attacks.

articles.title: Microsoft slashes Gears of War: E-Day price by a third just six weeks after launch
articles.description: Microsoft has cut the price of Gears of War: E-Day by 30% for Thanksgiving, with the discount running until December 2 on PC and Xbox Series X|S. The game only launched globally on October 6, so a cut of this size so soon is highly unusual for a major AAA release. Analysts estimate total sales of all versions at only around 400,000 copies by the end of October, pointing to a weak commercial start.
articles.body: Microsoft has temporarily cut the price of Gears of War: E-Day by 30%, with the Thanksgiving offer running until December 2 on PC and Xbox Series X|S. The game's global release was only on October 6, so a discount of a third just a month and a half after launch is a very unusual move for a big-budget AAA title. The decision is likely linked to low sales: according to analysts, combined sales of all versions of the game from The Coalition reached only about 400,000 copies by the end of October. Another factor may be the release of Grand Theft Auto VI, which is dominating attention and spending across the industry. Players have also been criticising the developers for ignoring problems and a lack of communication, a situation GameMAG notes echoes the one around Forza Horizon 6. The steep early discount suggests Microsoft is trying to widen the game's audience quickly rather than waiting for a slower seasonal sale.

articles.title: November PlayStation Plus games now available, led by Death Stranding 2: On the Beach
articles.description: Sony has made November's PlayStation Plus catalogue additions available to download on PS4 and PS5. The Extra tier gains seven games, headlined by Death Stranding 2: On the Beach, Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii and Dragon Quest III HD-2D Remake. Premium and Deluxe subscribers also get two classics: Soul Reaver 2 and Freedom Wars Remastered.
articles.body: Subscribers to the higher PlayStation Plus tiers can now download November's new catalogue games on PS4 and PS5. The PS Plus Extra library grows by seven titles: Hell Let Loose, Death Stranding 2: On the Beach, Atomfall, Dragon Quest III HD-2D Remake, Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii, Cricket 26: The Official Game of the Ashes, and Trepang2. The headliner is clearly Death Stranding 2: On the Beach, Hideo Kojima's sequel, which only released earlier this year, making its arrival in the subscription catalogue a fast one. The Premium and Deluxe tiers add two more classic games: Soul Reaver 2 and Freedom Wars Remastered. The November drop is a strong month for the service, mixing a major recent exclusive with a varied set of action, RPG and sports titles, and it lands just as the holiday season and the GTA VI launch dominate gaming attention.

articles.title: Hellraiser: Revival named Game of the Year at The Horror Game Awards 2026
articles.description: Clive Barker's Hellraiser: Revival has won Game of the Year at The Horror Game Awards 2026, beating favourite Resident Evil Requiem. The Saber Interactive horror game, which received no nominations at all at The Game Awards 2026, also earned Doug Bradley an award for Best Performance for his return as Pinhead. Resident Evil Requiem still took home the most prizes, with four wins.
articles.body: The Horror Game Awards 2026 has named its best horror games of the year, and the top prize went to an unexpected winner: Clive Barker's Hellraiser: Revival from Saber Interactive beat Resident Evil Requiem to Game of the Year. The Hellraiser game received no nominations at all at The Game Awards 2026, making the genre ceremony's recognition a notable contrast. Doug Bradley also won Best Performance for returning to the role of Pinhead, a character he first played in Clive Barker's original 1987 film. Resident Evil Requiem still collected the most awards overall, with four: Players' Choice, Best Narrative, Most Accessible Horror and Scariest Horror. The Silent Hill franchise was well represented too: Silent Hill Townfall won Critics' Choice, and Bloober Team's upcoming Silent Hill remake was named Most Anticipated Horror, while Bloober also took Best Developer. Other winners included Tenebris Somnia for Best Indie Horror and Best Art Direction, REANIMAL for Best New Multiplayer Horror, and a lifetime achievement award for longtime Silent Hill composer Akira Yamaoka.

articles.title: Insider: troubled Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic remake to be re-revealed at The Game Awards 2026
articles.description: Saber Interactive is reportedly planning to re-reveal the long-troubled remake of Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic at The Game Awards 2026, which airs on December 10. Insider Luke Hall of the 100% Star Wars channel says the plan has been in place since January and was recently confirmed by his sources. The remake was first announced in 2021 and moved from Aspyr to Saber after production problems.
articles.body: The long-troubled remake of Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic may finally come out of hiding at The Game Awards 2026, according to insider Luke Hall of the YouTube channel 100% Star Wars. Hall says Saber Interactive plans a repeat announcement of the remake during the ceremony, whose broadcast is scheduled for December 10, and that the plan was set as far back as January and recently confirmed by his sources. The remake was first unveiled in 2021 at a PlayStation presentation, developed by Aspyr Media, but production problems saw the project move to Saber Interactive, and almost nothing has been shown since. In March 2026, Hall said he had seen work on the remake and was impressed, and Saber creative director Tim Willits confirmed the same month that the game was still in development, without sharing details. A new showing would reportedly kick off a full marketing campaign, though Saber's business development director Steve Ellison has previously hinted at a release no earlier than 2028. A second Star Wars project from the same era, Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic from Casey Hudson's studio Arcanaut, could also appear at the show.

articles.title: GTA VI earns $3.79 billion in its first day, the biggest entertainment launch in history
articles.description: Take-Two has confirmed that Grand Theft Auto VI made $3.79 billion in retail sales on its first day, setting a new record for entertainment in any medium. The figure, announced on November 20, adds the key detail to the launch story: the game had already sold 32.5 million copies before release. For comparison, GTA V needed three days to reach $1 billion back in 2013.
articles.body: Take-Two Interactive and Rockstar Games have announced that Grand Theft Auto VI earned $3.79 billion in retail sales on its first day, making it the biggest entertainment launch in history across any medium. The official figure, released on November 20 and based on company estimates through the end of release day, November 19, is the major new detail on a launch already known for its record 32.5 million pre-release copies sold. The $3.79 billion first-day total is more than four times what GTA V managed: in 2013 the previous game needed three days to reach $1 billion. Independent estimates tell a similar story of scale: SensorTower put first-day sales and pre-orders above $2.36 billion with more than 24.58 million copies sold, with PlayStation players accounting for about $1.77 billion and Xbox players about $588 million. The game holds a near-perfect 99 on Metacritic. GTA VI is available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S at $80 for the standard edition and $100 for the Ultimate edition, with no desktop version yet and its date still to be announced.

articles.title: Ubisoft spins off AI team into Motherbrain subsidiary to build NPCs with memory and AI game masters
articles.description: Ubisoft has turned its generative AI unit into a separate subsidiary called Motherbrain, announced in its half-year earnings report on November 19. The team will build technology for non-player characters that remember past encounters with the player, and for AI 'game masters' that run living game worlds. It grows out of the Teammates voice-command experiment and the Neo NPC prototype.
articles.body: Ubisoft has spun off its Motherbrain unit into a separate subsidiary company that will develop generative AI technology for games, the publisher confirmed in its financial report for the first half of the 2026-27 fiscal year, published November 19. Motherbrain's goal is to make virtual worlds more interactive, with two main directions: behaviour models for NPCs that can remember past meetings with the player and take them into account in the next conversation, and AI systems that manage events in the game world, which the company calls a 'game master' by analogy with the host of a tabletop role-playing game. The team builds on earlier work: the Teammates tech demo, in which players gave voice orders to AI companions, and the Neo NPC prototype shown in 2024, where characters formed unique replies from their given personalities and backstories. Ubisoft plans to make Motherbrain's work a shared technology base for its internal studios and eventually for outside creators as well. The announcement came alongside continued cost-cutting, with reports of 166 job cuts in Montreal and Quebec City, while the same earnings report highlighted strong sales of Assassin's Creed Black Flag RE:Synchro and net bookings of 388.9 million euros for July to September, above guidance.

articles.title: Konami revives memories of Silent Scope and Thrill Drive with new trademark filings
articles.description: Konami has filed trademarks for the names of two classic series, Silent Scope and Thrill Drive, sparking speculation about revivals. Silent Scope was the company's light-gun sniper arcade series, while Thrill Drive was its driving game. No new game has been announced, so for now the filings are only a sign that Konami is dusting off its back catalogue.
articles.body: Konami has registered trademarks for the titles of two classic series, Silent Scope and Thrill Drive, according to new filings reported on November 21. Silent Scope is the light-gun sniper series that began in arcades, where players took the role of a sniper picking off targets through a rifle scope, while Thrill Drive was Konami's arcade-style driving game. Trademark filings do not by themselves confirm new games, and Konami has announced nothing, but the move fits a wider pattern of the publisher returning to its older franchises, as it has done with Silent Hill and other series in recent years. For now fans can only speculate whether the filings point to remakes, remasters or entirely new entries, or are simply defensive registrations to protect the names. Either way, the reappearance of two dormant brands from Konami's arcade era is a small but telling sign of how much value publishers now see in their back catalogues.

articles.title: Trump brushes off concerns about Witkoff after leaked transcript shows envoy coaching Putin aide
articles.description: President Trump has dismissed concerns about his special envoy Steve Witkoff after Bloomberg published a transcript of an October 14 call in which Witkoff coached Vladimir Putin's aide Yuri Ushakov on how to pitch a Ukraine peace plan to Trump. In the call Witkoff suggested Putin congratulate Trump on the Gaza ceasefire, praise him as a 'man of peace', and said a deal would take Donetsk and 'maybe a land swap somewhere'. Trump called the approach standard negotiating procedure.
articles.body: President Donald Trump has brushed off concerns about his special envoy Steve Witkoff after Bloomberg published a transcript of a phone call in which Witkoff advised a top Kremlin official on how to lobby Trump over a Ukraine peace plan. In the five-minute call on October 14, Witkoff told Putin's senior foreign-policy aide Yuri Ushakov that Putin should call Trump to congratulate him on the Gaza ceasefire deal, praise him as a 'man of peace', and then pivot to a 20-point Ukraine framework modelled on the Gaza agreement. Speaking 'between us', Witkoff added that he knew what it would take to clinch a deal: Russia getting Donetsk and 'maybe a land swap somewhere', language that aligns with long-standing Kremlin demands for Ukrainian territorial concessions. Trump, asked about the transcript aboard Air Force One, said he had not listened to the recording but described it as routine diplomacy, saying 'He's gotta sell this to Ukraine, he's gotta sell Ukraine to Russia. That's what a deal maker does.' The leak has roiled Washington: some Republican Russia hawks said Witkoff favours the Russians, and Representative Don Bacon called for him to be fired, while the Kremlin's Kirill Dmitriev called the leaks fake. A second leaked recording showed Ushakov discussing the 28-point US-Russian peace plan with Dmitriev. Trump said the peace proposal has been 'fine-tuned' and announced he is sending Witkoff to meet Putin in Moscow.

articles.title: Tai Po fire inquiry submits final report, blaming four Hong Kong government bodies
articles.description: A judge-led inquiry into Hong Kong's deadliest fire in decades has submitted its final report to the government, singling out four government bodies for accountability. The blaze at the Wang Fuk Court estate in Tai Po on November 26, 2025 killed 168 people, including a firefighter, and displaced nearly 5,000 residents. A redacted version of the report could be made public as early as next week.
articles.body: The independent committee investigating the Wang Fuk Court fire in Hong Kong's Tai Po district has submitted its final report to Chief Executive John Lee, almost a year after the blaze killed 168 people, including a firefighter, and displaced nearly 5,000 residents. The report, spanning more than ten chapters, singles out four government bodies for accountability — the Fire Services Department, the Buildings Department, the Labour Department and the Housing Bureau's Independent Checking Unit — as well as individual civil servants, and includes recommendations on construction material standards and measures to combat bid-rigging. Chaired by High Court judge David Lok Kai-hong, the panel held 30 public sessions from March, heard about 80 witnesses and collected over a million files; its lead counsel identified six 'human failures' behind the disaster. The Chief Executive has said the government bore 'unshirkable responsibility' for the tragedy, in which fire tore through seven of the estate's eight towers during renovation works. Prosecutions are already under way against seven individuals and two companies on 25 charges, including suspected manslaughter, conspiracy to defraud and attempting to pervert the course of justice. A redacted version of the report could be released as early as next week, with the full text held back until criminal proceedings conclude. A steering committee overseeing reforms after the fire held its first meeting on November 16.

articles.title: The boy making all the right moves in India's chess revolution
articles.description: Eight-year-old Tamizh Amudhan kept playing his chess match against one of the best players in the world even after a thunderstorm cut the power and the lights went out. His story captures India's remarkable chess boom, which has turned the country into a powerhouse of the game. The spotlight now turns to world champion Gukesh, who begins defending his title at the World Chess Championship in Geneva on Tuesday, November 24.
articles.body: The lights were out after a thunderstorm cut the power, but eight-year-old Tamizh Amudhan had a chess match to play against one of the best players in the world, and he played on. His determination is emblematic of the chess revolution sweeping India, where the game has exploded in popularity and the country now produces a steady stream of young grandmasters and prodigies. India has gone from a chess backwater to a dominant force in the space of a generation, with academies, online play and the example of its stars drawing millions of children to the board. The focus of that boom is world champion Gukesh Dommaraju, who became the youngest world champion in history and will begin defending his title at the World Chess Championship in Geneva on Tuesday, November 24. The championship is the biggest test yet of whether India's new generation can hold the crown it worked so hard to win, and stories like Amudhan's suggest the pipeline of talent behind Gukesh is only getting deeper.

articles.title: East Coast storm could disrupt holiday travel after battering Florida
articles.description: The same storm that flooded Florida's Atlantic coast this week is tracking up the East Coast, threatening one of the busiest holiday travel weekends of the year. Coastal areas from the Carolinas to southern New England face rain, localised flooding and gusty winds that could delay flights. Conditions worsen on Sunday, and another storm could hit the East Coast on Wednesday into Thanksgiving Day itself.
articles.body: The same stormy mess that flooded Florida's Atlantic coast this week is tracking up the East Coast, putting a damper on one of the busiest holiday travel weekends of the year. Coastal areas from the Carolinas to southern New England will feel the most significant impacts, including rain that could cause localised flooding and gusty winds that could delay flights. Rain and wind were already under way in parts of the Carolinas, with widespread gusts around 20 mph and some closer to 40 mph along the coast, and travel conditions in the Mid-Atlantic were expected to deteriorate on Sunday as rain spreads north. Flights from Philadelphia's and New York's airports should avoid most weather issues on Sunday morning, but rain and gusty winds arriving in the Northeast in the afternoon and evening could also slow road travel, including the heavily travelled Interstate 95 corridor from Virginia to New York City. More weather trouble is possible later in the week: another storm could affect the East Coast on Wednesday into Thanksgiving Day, potentially bringing a very wet and windy holiday to the Mid-Atlantic and parts of the Northeast, including New York City, home to the iconic Thanksgiving parade. The West Coast faces disruption too, with light rain and high-elevation snow in the Pacific Northwest this weekend and a new storm set to arrive late Monday into Tuesday.

articles.title: GPS collars reveal 'strange prey' for some of Thailand's last tigers
articles.description: Conservationists in Thailand have fitted GPS collars to three of the last Indochinese tigers in the Dong Phayayen-Khao Yai Forest Complex, and the data holds a surprise: the tigers are hunting unusually small prey. Instead of large animals like banteng, gaur or sambar deer, the cats are eating wild pigs and muntjac deer as small as 10 kilograms, a sign that large prey is scarce in the forest. Only 20 to 30 tigers remain in the 6,000-square-kilometre complex.
articles.body: Deep in the evergreen jungle of Thailand's Dong Phayayen-Khao Yai Forest Complex, conservationists are using GPS collars to track the eating habits of the country's last remaining Indochinese tigers, and what they found was unexpected. With just 20 to 30 tigers roaming the 6,000-square-kilometre forest complex, a population only discovered in the early 2000s, the team from Thailand's Department of National Parks and the nonprofit Panthera fitted collars to three tigers in early 2025: an adult male named Srikosa and sub-adult sisters Chantra and Pianporn. The lightweight collars record coordinates every hour, have a battery life of up to two years, and detach automatically when the battery runs low. By following the tigers to their kill sites, researchers discovered the cats were eating 'strange prey': small mammals like wild pigs and muntjac deer, some weighing as little as 10 kilograms, rather than the large banteng, gaur or sambar deer of up to 350 kilograms that tigers typically hunt. The finding reinforces a study from last year highlighting the limited number of large prey in the forest, and it could reflect the scarcity of big ungulates in the complex. The work sits within a wider Thai success story: the country's wild tiger population is estimated at 210 to 257 animals, making Thailand the only country in Southeast Asia with a sustained rise in tiger numbers, helped by prey-release programmes and camera-trap monitoring.

articles.title: TikTok says 94% of songs that entered the Billboard Global 200 in 2025 went viral on its platform first
articles.description: TikTok's 2026 Music Impact Report, prepared with Luminate, claims 94% of the songs that entered the Billboard Global 200 in 2025 went viral on TikTok before charting, up from 84% in 2024. The figure underlines how central the short-video app has become to breaking new music worldwide. For labels and artists, it means a TikTok moment is now less a bonus and more a precondition for global chart success.
articles.body: TikTok says 94% of the songs that entered the Billboard Global 200 in 2025 went viral on its platform first, according to the platform's 2026 Music Impact Report, which was prepared by Luminate and published on November 18. That share is up from 84% in 2024, a sharp rise in a single year. The report positions TikTok not just as a discovery channel but as the main launchpad for global hits, ahead of radio, playlists and traditional press. For the music business, the finding sharpens a familiar tension: labels increasingly depend on a platform they do not control, and whose algorithm can make or stall a release overnight. It also raises the stakes of TikTok's commercial negotiations with the majors, since the app can credibly claim to be the gatekeeper of global chart entry. Independent artists, meanwhile, face a landscape where a viral clip can do more for a song than a full marketing campaign. The report lands as TikTok continues to expand its own music tools, including its in-app streaming service in some markets. Whether the 94% figure holds in 2026 will be watched closely, but the direction of travel is clear: virality on TikTok is now the default route to the world's biggest chart.

articles.title: NetEase Cloud Music's Q3 revenues fell 0.9% YoY to $290m after subscription revenues grew 5.3% in H1
articles.description: NetEase Cloud Music's revenues slipped 0.9% year on year to around $290 million in the third quarter, even though the Chinese streamer re-signed licensing deals with all three major labels this year. Subscription revenue growth has slowed to roughly a third of its pace a year earlier. The slowdown shows how hard it is to keep growing paid music subscriptions in China's crowded, price-sensitive market.
articles.body: NetEase Cloud Music reported third-quarter revenues of around $290 million, down 0.9% year on year, in a softer set of results for China's second-biggest music streamer. The company re-signed licensing agreements with all three major labels this year, securing its catalogue, but that has not translated into faster growth. Subscription revenue growth has slowed to roughly a third of the pace it managed a year earlier, after rising 5.3% in the first half. The figures point to a maturing Chinese streaming market, where competition with Tencent Music is intense and users are reluctant to pay more for subscriptions. NetEase has leaned on social and community features, live streaming and its indie artist ecosystem to differentiate itself, but monetising those features at scale remains a challenge. The results will be watched by the majors, for whom China is a long-term growth bet that has yet to deliver streaming economics comparable to the West. For now, NetEase's story is one of a solid but slowing business in a market where the easy subscriber growth has already been won.

articles.title: UMG and Sony withdraw DistroKid subpoena motion in Suno case after distributor produces AI-detection documents
articles.description: Universal Music Group and Sony Music have withdrawn their motion to subpoena DistroKid in their copyright case against AI music generator Suno, after the distributor handed over documents about how it detects AI-generated tracks. The labels had sought data on how many DistroKid tracks were flagged as AI-generated, how many were attributed to Suno, and what they earned. The withdrawal narrows one front of the labels' wider legal campaign against AI training on copyrighted music.
articles.body: Universal Music Group and Sony Music have withdrawn their motion to force distributor DistroKid to hand over documents in their copyright infringement case against AI music company Suno. The labels had sought data on how many tracks distributed by DistroKid were flagged as AI-generated, how many of those were attributed to Suno, and how much money they earned. DistroKid has now produced AI-detection documents, prompting the labels to drop the subpoena request. The episode is a side battle in the majors' much larger fight with Suno and fellow AI generator Udio, whom they accuse of training models on copyrighted recordings without permission. The data the labels wanted would have helped quantify how much AI-generated music is already flowing through distribution pipelines and earning royalties. DistroKid sits in the middle of that flow as one of the largest distributors for independent artists, making its detection practices a key piece of evidence. The withdrawal does not end the main Suno case, which remains one of the most consequential copyright fights in music. But it shows the labels are willing to de-escalate procedural skirmishes once they get the information they need, keeping the focus on the core question of whether AI training on copyrighted music is infringement.

articles.title: Pophouse appoints Oak View Group's Kristina Heney and Netflix's Greg Lombardo as Presidents
articles.description: Pophouse, the Swedish entertainment company behind ABBA Voyage, has appointed Kristina Heney from Oak View Group as President, Commercial & Marketing, and Greg Lombardo from Netflix as President of the Pophouse Avatar Network. The hires signal Pophouse's ambition to scale its avatar-concert model beyond ABBA. It is a notable executive shuffle at the intersection of live entertainment, streaming and virtual performance.
articles.body: Pophouse has appointed Kristina Heney and Greg Lombardo as Presidents in a double hire that signals the company's ambitions to grow beyond its flagship ABBA Voyage show. Heney joins from Oak View Group as President, Commercial & Marketing, while Lombardo arrives from Netflix as President of the Pophouse Avatar Network. Pophouse, founded in Stockholm, built its reputation on ABBA Voyage, the London residency in which digital avatars of the Swedish group perform with a live band, a format that has become one of the most successful new live-entertainment products of recent years. Heney's background in venue and live-entertainment commercial strategy at Oak View Group points to a push to commercialise Pophouse's formats more aggressively. Lombardo's Netflix pedigree and his new remit over the Avatar Network suggest the company wants to turn avatar concerts into a repeatable, global business rather than a one-off spectacle. The appointments come as other artists explore digital likeness performances, and as the economics of touring make virtual residencies increasingly attractive. For Pophouse, the challenge now is proving that the ABBA model can work for other catalogues and other artists.

articles.title: Switzerland's MusicBird secures up to $200M revolving credit facility arranged by Truist and Fifth Third
articles.description: Swiss music-rights company MusicBird has secured a revolving credit facility of up to $200 million, arranged by Truist and Fifth Third. The company says the new financing will help it scale its portfolio of music rights. The deal is the latest sign that debt markets remain open to music-catalogue buyers even as interest rates stay high.
articles.body: Switzerland's MusicBird has secured a revolving credit facility of up to $200 million, arranged by Truist and Fifth Third, in a deal that underlines continued lender appetite for music rights. MusicBird says the new financing will help it scale its portfolio, giving it firepower to acquire more catalogues and royalty streams. Revolving credit facilities have become a standard tool for music-rights companies, letting them draw down funds for acquisitions and repay as royalties come in. The involvement of two major US banks is notable: it suggests institutional lenders still view music royalties as a relatively stable, uncorrelated asset class, despite higher interest rates and a cooling in some parts of the catalogue market. MusicBird is a newer entrant compared with giants like Hipgnosis and Concord, but the size of the facility signals serious ambitions. The deal also reflects a broader trend of European music companies tapping US debt markets to fund growth. For artists and rights-holders considering a sale, the message is that buyers still have access to capital, even if the frothy valuations of a few years ago have moderated.

articles.title: Live experiences platform Speakeasy, backed by Yamaha's music fund, raises $18.8M Series A
articles.description: Speakeasy, a platform for live experiences backed by Yamaha's music fund, has raised an $18.8 million Series A, bringing its total funding to about $27 million. The company builds tools around in-person music and cultural experiences. The raise shows investors still see room for new live-experience platforms even as the post-pandemic live boom matures.
articles.body: Live experiences platform Speakeasy has raised an $18.8 million Series A round, bringing its total funding to approximately $27 million. The company is backed by Yamaha's music fund, a notable vote of confidence from one of the music industry's biggest instrument and technology companies. Speakeasy operates in the live-experiences space, building products around in-person music and cultural events at a time when audiences are spending heavily on going out. The funding comes as the live sector digests a huge post-pandemic boom and looks for the next wave of growth, including better discovery, ticketing and fan-experience tools. Yamaha's involvement is interesting because it connects an instrument maker with the live-experience economy, a pairing that could open distribution and partnership routes. For a startup, $18.8 million is a substantial Series A and suggests investors believe there is still whitespace in how fans find and attend live events. The challenge for Speakeasy will be converting that capital into a durable position against entrenched ticketing and event platforms.

articles.title: $11M-backed AI startup Sonilo, founded by TikTok veterans, inks licensing deal with Symphonic to train its model on opted-in indie recordings
articles.description: Sonilo, an AI music startup founded by TikTok veterans and backed with $11 million, has signed a licensing deal with distributor Symphonic to train its AI model on recordings from independent artists and labels — but only those that opt in. The deal is a rare example of a licensed, consent-based approach to AI music training, in contrast to the unlicensed training alleged in the Suno and Udio lawsuits. It could become a template for how AI companies and the indie sector work together.
articles.body: AI music startup Sonilo, founded by TikTok veterans and backed with $11 million, has signed a licensing deal with Symphonic that allows it to train its AI model on recordings from the distributor's independent artists and labels — but only those that choose to opt in. The agreement is a deliberate contrast to the approach taken by Suno and Udio, which the major labels accuse of training on copyrighted music without permission. By building an opt-in catalogue, Sonilo is betting that consent-based training can be both legally safe and commercially viable, and that indie artists will participate if they are paid and credited. Symphonic, which distributes music for a large roster of independent labels, gains a new revenue stream for its artists and a stake in shaping how AI uses their work. The deal also reflects the growing split in the AI music world between companies seeking licences and those fighting lawsuits. For the indie sector, the opt-in model offers a way to benefit from AI rather than simply being its raw material. Whether enough artists opt in to make Sonilo's model competitive remains an open question, but the deal is a meaningful proof of concept for licensed AI training.

articles.title: Vevo dscvr Artists to Watch 2027: Dalvin La Melodía, Conep, Devon Again, Mari Froes, Die Spitz
articles.description: Vevo has unveiled the first batch of its dscvr Artists to Watch for 2027, naming Dalvin La Melodía, Conep, Devon Again, Mari Froes and Die Spitz. The annual list is one of the music-video platform's main tastemaker franchises, spotlighting emerging acts it expects to break through. For the five artists, the nod brings Vevo's global video reach and promotional muscle.
articles.body: Vevo has introduced the first batch of its dscvr Artists to Watch for 2027, naming Dalvin La Melodía, Conep, Devon Again, Mari Froes and Die Spitz. The dscvr franchise is Vevo's long-running emerging-artist programme, built around exclusive live performances filmed for the platform, and its annual Artists to Watch list has become a reliable early indicator of breakout talent. The five acts span genres and geographies, reflecting Vevo's global footprint and its attempt to catch artists before they cross over. For the artists, inclusion means prominent placement across Vevo's network, which reaches hundreds of millions of viewers through YouTube and connected TV. The programme matters to the industry because Vevo's editorial choices are closely watched by labels, playlist editors and sync supervisors looking for the next wave. The first batch will be followed by further announcements as the 2027 list fills out. For fans, it is an early playlist of names to watch; for the artists, it is a stamp of approval from one of music video's most influential platforms.

articles.title: Rosalía calls Taylor Swift a 'master songwriter,' reveals her favorite Swift track
articles.description: Rosalía has praised Taylor Swift as a 'master songwriter' and revealed her favorite Swift track, in a warm public exchange between two of pop's biggest stars. The Spanish singer's comments add to a long run of mutual admiration between the two artists. It is the kind of cross-generational pop moment that tends to travel far on social media.
articles.body: Rosalía has called Taylor Swift a 'master songwriter' and revealed her favorite Swift track, in the latest warm exchange between two of the biggest stars in pop. The Spanish singer, whose own work blends flamenco, reggaeton and experimental pop, has long been vocal about her admiration for Swift's craft, and the new comments underline a mutual respect that fans of both artists have followed for years. Swift, for her part, has previously praised Rosalía's artistry, making the exchange one of pop's friendlier high-profile relationships. The moment lands as both artists continue to dominate the global pop conversation: Swift with her latest album era and Rosalía with her own acclaimed recent work. Such endorsements matter in pop, where a compliment from a peer can carry as much weight as a review. For Rosalía, aligning herself publicly with Swift's songwriting also reinforces her own ambitions as a writer, not just a performer. The story has been picked up widely because it is a rare, uncomplicatedly positive moment between two superstars who rarely share a stage but clearly share an audience.

articles.title: Unreleased D'Angelo song 'Kamakazi' emerges in 'GTA VI'
articles.description: An unreleased D'Angelo song, 'Kamakazi,' has surfaced in Grand Theft Auto VI, giving fans a first hearing of new material from the late soul singer. The track's appearance in the year's biggest video game is a striking posthumous moment. It also underlines how GTA has become one of music's most powerful discovery platforms.
articles.body: An unreleased D'Angelo song titled 'Kamakazi' has emerged in Grand Theft Auto VI, offering fans their first listen to previously unheard material from the soul singer. The track appears in the game, which is the most anticipated entertainment release of the year, and its inclusion immediately became one of the most talked-about music moments around the launch. D'Angelo, who died earlier this year, left behind a small but hugely influential catalogue, and any unreleased recording carries enormous weight for his fans. The song's appearance in GTA VI also shows how the franchise has become a tastemaker in its own right: its radio stations and soundtrack placements have launched and revived careers for two decades. Rockstar Games has a history of using the series to spotlight soul, funk and hip-hop deep cuts alongside new music. For D'Angelo's estate and label, the placement is a high-profile way to keep his legacy in front of a new generation. Whether 'Kamakazi' gets a standalone release remains to be seen, but its debut inside the biggest game of the year guarantees it an audience of millions.

articles.title: Harry Styles, Sam Fender, Billie Eilish and Cher to headline Glastonbury 2027
articles.description: Glastonbury has announced its 2027 headliners: Harry Styles, Sam Fender and Billie Eilish will top the Pyramid Stage, with Cher taking the Sunday afternoon Legends slot. The festival returns after its traditional fallow year in 2026. Styles and Fender will headline for the first time, while Eilish returns after making history in 2022 as the youngest solo headliner.
articles.body: Glastonbury Festival has announced its 2027 lineup, with Harry Styles, Sam Fender and Billie Eilish headlining and Cher taking the prestigious Sunday afternoon Legends slot. The festival returns to Worthy Farm in Somerset from June 23 to 27, with the main music programme running June 25 to 27, after taking its traditional fallow year in 2026 to let the land recover. Styles, who recently completed a 30-show residency at Madison Square Garden in New York, will play Glastonbury for the first time as a solo headliner, and has previously credited the festival's dance area with inspiring his album 'Kiss All The Time. Disco, Occasionally.' Fender will also top the bill for the first time after a huge year, while Eilish returns to the Pyramid Stage after making history in 2022 as the festival's youngest-ever solo headliner. Cher, at 81, takes the Legends slot, one of the most beloved traditions in the Glastonbury weekend. The undercard is stacked, with Massive Attack, Chase & Status, The xx, Lily Allen, Ezra Collective, Kraftwerk, FKA twigs, Robyn, Underworld, The War on Drugs and King Gizzard and the Lizard Wizard among the acts announced. Glastonbury sells out before headliners are named, so the announcement is less about tickets than about setting the tone for the summer's biggest festival weekend.

articles.title: Julio Iglesias under investigation for sexual abuse claims
articles.description: Spanish singer Julio Iglesias is under investigation over sexual abuse claims, Rolling Stone reports. The news is a serious development for one of the best-selling Latin artists of all time. Details of the investigation are still emerging, and Iglesias has not yet publicly responded in the reporting so far.
articles.body: Julio Iglesias, one of the best-selling Latin music artists of all time, is under investigation over sexual abuse claims, according to Rolling Stone. The report marks a grave development for the 83-year-old Spanish singer, whose career spans more than five decades and hundreds of millions of records sold worldwide. Iglesias is a towering figure in Latin pop and romantic balladry, with a global audience built since the 1970s, and any investigation into his conduct is likely to reverberate across the Spanish-speaking music world. The specifics of the claims and the jurisdiction handling the investigation are still emerging, and the reporting so far does not indicate charges have been filed. Iglesias has not yet publicly responded to the claims in the coverage to date. The story arrives in an era when legacy artists are increasingly facing scrutiny over past conduct, and when the music industry's handling of abuse allegations is under sustained pressure. Further details, including any statement from Iglesias or his representatives, are expected as the investigation develops.

articles.title: Bruno Mars mourns his father's death: 'The man that taught me everything I know'
articles.description: Bruno Mars has announced the death of his father, Peter Hernandez, paying tribute to 'the man that taught me everything I know.' Hernandez was a musician and entertainer who shaped his son's early life in music. The announcement has drawn an outpouring of condolences from fans and fellow artists.
articles.body: Bruno Mars has announced the death of his father, Peter Hernandez, with a tribute calling him 'the man that taught me everything I know.' Hernandez was a musician and entertainer in his own right, a percussionist and Elvis impersonator who performed in Hawaii, where Mars grew up immersed in live music from childhood. Mars has often credited his father with his musical education, from stagecraft to showmanship, and the family's performing roots are central to the story of how he became one of pop's most complete entertainers. The announcement was shared with fans, who responded with an outpouring of condolences, and fellow artists have also paid tribute. Hernandez's influence is audible in Mars's work: the retro showmanship, the live-band energy and the deep knowledge of soul, funk and rock and roll. The news comes as Mars remains one of the world's most in-demand live acts. No further details about funeral arrangements have been shared publicly, and the family has asked for privacy as they grieve.

articles.title: Beastie Boys' Mike D brings solo album — and his sons — to Tiny Desk Concert
articles.description: Beastie Boys' Mike D has brought his new solo album to NPR's Tiny Desk Concert, performing with his sons in a family affair. The appearance marks a rare solo spotlight for the rapper, decades after the Beastie Boys became hip-hop legends. It is a warm, personal performance that doubles as a passing of the torch.
articles.body: Beastie Boys' Mike D has taken his solo album to NPR's Tiny Desk Concert, performing alongside his sons in a set that blends new material with the weight of hip-hop history. The appearance is a rare solo turn for Michael Diamond, who with Adam 'Ad-Rock' Horovitz and the late Adam 'MCA' Yauch built the Beastie Boys into one of the most inventive and enduring acts in rap. The Tiny Desk format, stripped-back and intimate, suits a reflective set, and the presence of his sons adds a generational dimension to the performance. The Beastie Boys' legacy has been carefully tended since MCA's death in 2012, through the bestselling memoir, the documentary and archival releases, but a new solo album from Mike D is a genuinely fresh chapter. The Tiny Desk appearance gives the record a high-profile launchpad with an audience that spans hip-hop lifers and younger listeners discovering the group through streaming. It also underlines how the Tiny Desk has become a rite of passage for legacy artists with something new to say.

articles.title: Foo Fighters, Noah Kahan, the Who lead New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival lineup
articles.description: Foo Fighters, Noah Kahan and the Who will headline the New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival, anchoring one of America's most storied festival lineups. The announcement sets up a big spring weekend at the Fair Grounds. The mix of rock legends and a modern folk star reflects the festival's broad, genre-spanning identity.
articles.body: Foo Fighters, Noah Kahan and the Who will lead the lineup of the New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival, one of America's most beloved and storied music events. The announcement puts three very different headliners at the top of a bill that traditionally spans jazz, blues, gospel, Cajun, rock and hip-hop across seven stages at the Fair Grounds Race Course. The Foo Fighters bring arena-rock scale to a festival that has increasingly mixed legacy rock acts with its Louisiana roots. The Who, now deep into their farewell era, add another chapter to a long relationship with American festival stages. Noah Kahan represents the newer generation, a folk-pop star whose rise from Vermont to festival headliner has been one of the defining commercial stories of the last few years. Jazz Fest is as much a cultural institution as a music festival, with food, crafts and local traditions as central as the music itself. The full lineup will fill out over the coming weeks, but the headliners already set the tone: a weekend that bridges generations and genres, in the city where so much of American music began.

articles.title: Lil Baby's 'FRESH' debuts at No. 2 on Billboard 200 with 59,000 units, topping streaming chart
articles.description: Lil Baby's new album 'FRESH' debuted at No. 2 on the Billboard 200 dated November 21, earning 59,000 equivalent album units — just 3,000 behind Olivia Rodrigo at No. 1. He won the streaming race with 56.81 million on-demand streams, topping the Top Streaming Albums chart, but sold only 4,000 copies. It is his eighth top 10 album, and all eight have debuted in the top five.
articles.body: Lil Baby's 'FRESH' debuted at No. 2 on the Billboard 200 dated November 21, 2026, earning 59,000 equivalent album units in the tracking week ending November 12, according to Luminate data reported by Billboard. The album finished just 3,000 units behind Olivia Rodrigo's chart-topper, making it one of the closest chart races of the season. The twist is that Lil Baby actually won the streaming battle: 'FRESH' generated 55,000 streaming equivalent units, equal to 56.81 million on-demand official streams, enough to debut at No. 1 on Top Streaming Albums. What kept him from the top spot was pure sales — just 4,000 copies, good for only a No. 33 debut on Top Album Sales. 'FRESH' is Lil Baby's eighth top 10 album, and remarkably, all eight have debuted inside the top five. The album, announced on October 20 and released on November 6, was preceded by lead single 'Dead Fresh,' which became his 28th top 20 hit on the Hot 100. Eight of the album's tracks also debuted on the Hot 100 this week, taking his career total to 168 entries, the seventh-highest tally in the chart's history. The result captures the modern chart dynamic: streaming dominance alone is no longer enough to guarantee No. 1 when a rival can convert sales.

articles.title: Remi Wolf earns first Billboard No. 1 as 'Bottle' tops Adult Alternative Airplay
articles.description: Remi Wolf has earned the first Billboard No. 1 of her career, as her single 'Bottle' rises to the top of the Adult Alternative Airplay chart dated November 28. The song climbed from No. 2 with a 13% increase in spins during the tracking week of November 13-19. It is the second single from her third album 'Mud,' which reached No. 18 on the Billboard 200 in October.
articles.body: Remi Wolf has earned the first Billboard No. 1 of her career, as her single 'Bottle' rises to the top of the Adult Alternative Airplay chart dated November 28, 2026. The song climbed from No. 2 with a 13% increase in spins at the format during the tracking week of November 13 to 19, according to Luminate data reported by Billboard.
