The two-stage lineup includes a Cactus Jack set with Travis Scott, Don Toliver, Kodak Black and SoFaygo, plus Cardi B, Justice (DJ set), Metro Boomin, Rauw & Friends and Tainy. All ticket-sale proceeds go to nine local Miami charities.
articles.body: Rockstar Games and PlayStation stage Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival tonight, November 21, at Mana Wynwood in Miami, two days after the game's record-breaking launch. The two-stage lineup includes a Cactus Jack set with Travis Scott, Don Toliver, Kodak Black and SoFaygo, plus Cardi B, Justice (DJ set), Metro Boomin, Rauw & Friends and Tainy — a bill drawn straight from the game's soundtrack world. Rockstar confirmed all ticket-sale proceeds go to nine local Miami charities, including The Miami Foundation and the Coconut Grove Crisis Food Pantry. The festival turns a game launch into a live event, bringing the Vice City universe into the real Miami that inspired it. For Rockstar, it is a victory lap two days after the biggest entertainment launch in history. For Miami, it is a night of music with the money staying local.

articles.title: Future's surprise single 'Ya Hit' with Drake, Travis Scott and Loe Shimmy debuts at No. 38 on the Hot 100
articles.description: Future's surprise single 'Ya Hit,' featuring Drake, Travis Scott and Loe Shimmy, debuted at No. 38 on the Hot 100 and No. 23 on the Canadian Hot 100 in its first week. The video was shot at Houston strip club Area 29. Drake had five songs on the Canadian chart that week, led by his own entries.
articles.body: Future's surprise single 'Ya Hit,' featuring Drake, Travis Scott and Loe Shimmy, debuted at No. 38 on the Hot 100 and No. 23 on the Canadian Hot 100 in its first week. The video was shot at Houston strip club Area 29, keeping the visuals close to the song's world. The collaboration stacks three of hip-hop's biggest names on one track, with Loe Shimmy as the rising voice alongside them. Drake had five songs on the Canadian chart that week, led by his own entries, underlining his continued dominance at home. For Future, the debut is another chart entry in a year of steady releases; for the featured artists, it is a reminder of how much gravity a surprise drop still carries. The single's first-week numbers suggest it has room to climb.

articles.title: Julien Baker announces first solo album in six years, 'This World or the Next'
articles.description: Julien Baker has announced her first solo album in six years, 'This World or the Next,' due in February, with lead single 'Hound' out now. The announcement is the freshest news from Billboard's Best New Music Friday roundup, which is otherwise led by the GTA VI soundtrack album and Gracie Abrams' deluxe edition, both covered in yesterday's digest.
articles.body: Julien Baker has announced her first solo album in six years, 'This World or the Next,' due in February, with lead single 'Hound' out now. The announcement is the freshest news from Billboard's Best New Music Friday roundup, which is otherwise led by the 'Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album' soundtrack and Gracie Abrams' deluxe edition of 'Daughter From Hell' — both covered in yesterday's digest. Baker's return to solo work comes after years of collaboration, including her work with boygenius alongside Phoebe Bridgers and Lucy Dacus. Six years is a long gap for a solo artist, and the announcement has been met with anticipation from fans who have followed her since her debut. 'Hound' is the first taste of the new record, and it sets the tone for an album that arrives in February. For Baker, the solo return is a homecoming; for listeners, it is the start of a new chapter.

articles.title: U2's 'Carnaval de Luz' tops charts in Ireland and the UK; Down release first album since 2007
articles.description: U2's 'Carnaval de Luz' topped the charts in Ireland and the UK this week, while sludge-metal supergroup Down released 'Volume V,' their first album since 2007. The week's chart coverage also notes Michael Jackson's 'Thriller' holding at No. 10 on the Billboard 200 after its Halloween surge, and at No. 1 on the Vinyl Albums chart.
articles.body: U2's 'Carnaval de Luz' topped the charts in Ireland and the UK this week, a home-turf No. 1 for the Dublin band and a reminder of their enduring chart power. Meanwhile, sludge-metal supergroup Down released 'Volume V,' their first album since 2007 — a 19-year gap that makes the record an event for metal fans. The week's chart coverage also notes Michael Jackson's 'Thriller' holding at No. 10 on the Billboard 200 after its Halloween surge, and at No. 1 on the Vinyl Albums chart, where it continues to sell year after year. Three very different stories, one theme: catalogue and legacy acts still move the charts. U2 at No. 1, Down back after nearly two decades, and 'Thriller' refusing to leave — the week belonged to the veterans.

articles.title: Russian ballistic strike on Kryvyi Rih kills a 7-year-old boy and a young paramedic; 58 people injured
articles.description: Russia struck the centre of Kryvyi Rih with ballistic missiles on the evening of November 20, killing a 7-year-old boy and a 20-year-old ambulance paramedic, with the number of injured rising to 58 by the morning, including six children. The attack damaged a hospital, around 25 apartment blocks, schools and ambulances, and Russian drones later struck rescuers working at the scene. It matters because Kryvyi Rih is President Zelenskyy's home city and the strike on a hospital and residential blocks is the latest in Russia's campaign against civilian infrastructure as winter sets in.
articles.body: Russia attacked the centre of Kryvyi Rih with ballistic missiles on the evening of November 20, and by the morning of November 21 the toll stood at two dead and 58 injured, including six children, three ambulance medics and rescue workers. The dead were a 7-year-old boy and a 20-year-old paramedic who had come to help the wounded; a second paramedic was among those killed in later reports from the scene. The strike damaged a hospital, around 25 multi-storey residential buildings, educational institutions and ambulances, and fires broke out across the impact zone. Rescue work was carried out under the threat of repeat strikes, and Russian attack drones hit the rescue site twice, injuring more emergency workers. Overnight, a jet-powered Shahed drone also struck an industrial enterprise in the city, starting a large fire. Kryvyi Rih, in Dnipropetrovsk region, is President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's home city and has been hit repeatedly during the war, but the targeting of a hospital and the follow-up drone attacks on rescuers underline the deliberate cruelty of the latest strike. The attack came the same night Russia launched 3 ballistic missiles and 148 drones across Ukraine, and it followed the massive November 20 barrage on Kyiv that damaged three bridges across the Dnipro. For Ukraine, the Kryvyi Rih strike is a reminder that even as peace talks dominate the headlines in Shenzhen and Berlin, Russian missiles continue to kill children in Ukrainian cities.

articles.title: Justice wrote the GTA VI soundtrack — and the game has 22 radio stations, plus a secret 23rd
articles.description: The main soundtrack for Grand Theft Auto VI was written by French electronic duo Justice — Xavier de Rosnay and Gaspar Augé — Meduza reports in a feature on the game's music. The game, released on November 19, has 22 radio stations in the car, more than any previous Rockstar game, plus a hidden 23rd station, The Vault Radio, unlockable in a Vice City club. The companion album, 'Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album', came out on streaming on November 20, and a festival in Miami on November 21 celebrates the release.
articles.body: Grand Theft Auto VI is famous for its music, and the new instalment is musically richer than any before it, Meduza writes — the game's budget is roughly estimated at $1–1.5 billion. The main soundtrack, which plays during missions, was written by Xavier de Rosnay and Gaspar Augé, the French electronic musicians behind the celebrated electro-house duo Justice. Their score will be released in full on streaming and on physical media, CD and vinyl, on December 11. The radio is even bigger: there are 22 stations to choose from in the car, more than in any previous Rockstar game, covering a huge range of genres, and there is a hidden 23rd station, The Vault Radio, which can be unlocked in The Vault club in central Vice City. On November 20 the compilation 'Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album', made up mostly of tracks heard on the game's radio, arrived on streaming services. On November 21 Miami hosts a whole festival dedicated to the game's release and its soundtrack, Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival, featuring musicians from the album. The feature matters for players and music fans alike: GTA's radio has launched careers and revived old hits for two decades, and this time Rockstar has turned the soundtrack into a standalone cultural event, with one of electronic music's biggest acts at its centre.

articles.title: Denmark expels Russia's military attaché and tightens visas for Russian citizens
articles.description: Denmark will expel Russia's military attaché, who must leave the country within seven days, Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen announced — and Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen added that Denmark will sharply cut visa issuance to Russian citizens. The expulsion follows the arrest of two Danish citizens accused of plotting to assassinate Ukrainian rapper Kyivstoner, real name Albert Vasilyev. The new visa restrictions are the fresh development: Denmark will stop issuing all non-essential visas to Russians, and such visas will be valid only in the issuing country.
articles.body: Denmark has decided to expel Russia's military attaché, who must leave the country within seven days, Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen announced at a press conference. The decision followed the arrest of two Danish citizens accused of plotting to assassinate the Ukrainian rapper Kyivstoner, whose real name is Albert Vasilyev. According to the Russian Embassy's website, the attaché is Vladimir Grekov. The expulsion itself was reported on November 20; the new development is that Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen has now announced a further step, saying Denmark will tighten sanctions against Russia, including ending the issuance of all non-essential visas to Russian citizens, with such visas valid only in the country that issued them. The combined measures are a direct diplomatic response to what Danish authorities describe as a Russian-directed murder plot against a Ukrainian public figure living in exile. It fits a wider pattern of alleged Russian operations targeting Ukrainian and dissident figures across Europe, which have prompted a series of expulsions and prosecutions in recent years. The case also highlights the reach of such plots into Scandinavia, a region that has stepped up counterintelligence work since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine. For Kyiv, the Danish response is a sign that European governments are treating Russian operations on their soil as a direct security threat, not a distant war.

articles.title: I have no right to vote, as hundreds of millions of Russians don't': Zvyagintsev answers Peskov over his Cannes speech
articles.description: Director Andrei Zvyagintsev has replied to Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov, who refused to pass on to Vladimir Putin the speech Zvyagintsev gave at Cannes. Meduza publishes Zvyagintsev's answer, in which he says he has no right to vote, 'as hundreds of millions of Russians don't today'. The exchange is a rare public clash between one of Russia's most acclaimed filmmakers and the Kremlin.
articles.body: Film director Andrei Zvyagintsev has answered Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov, who refused to pass on to Vladimir Putin the words Zvyagintsev spoke at the Cannes Film Festival. Meduza asked Zvyagintsev to comment on Peskov's refusal, and publishes his reply. 'Yes, quite right — I have no right to vote, as hundreds of millions of Russians don't today,' Zvyagintsev said, in a pointed remark about the state of political participation in Russia. Zvyagintsev is one of Russia's most internationally acclaimed directors, known for films such as 'Leviathan' and 'Loveless', and his Cannes speech had evidently touched a nerve in the Kremlin. Peskov's refusal to relay the speech to the president is itself telling: rather than ignoring a critical voice, the Kremlin spokesman publicly declined to transmit it, turning a festival speech into a small political event. The exchange captures the position of Russia's remaining independent cultural figures, who can still speak abroad but whose words are blocked from reaching the top at home. It also shows how tightly the Kremlin now polices even indirect criticism from artists it once celebrated.

articles.title: Jellyfish shut down three of six reactors at France's biggest nuclear plant
articles.description: Three of the six reactors at Gravelines, France's largest nuclear power plant, have been stopped after jellyfish clogged the cooling systems, Reuters reports, citing plant operator EDF. It is a reminder that even the most advanced energy infrastructure can be knocked offline by nature. The plant's operator says the shutdowns are precautionary and the reactors will return to service once the cooling intakes are cleared.
articles.body: Three of the six nuclear reactors at Gravelines, the largest nuclear power station in France, have been stopped because jellyfish accumulated in the cooling systems, Reuters reported, citing a statement from the plant's operator EDF. The jellyfish blocked the water intakes that cool the reactors, forcing the precautionary shutdowns until the systems can be cleared. Gravelines, on the French coast near Dunkirk, is one of the biggest nuclear plants in Europe, and the incident is a vivid reminder that even highly engineered energy infrastructure remains vulnerable to the natural world. Jellyfish blooms have caused similar shutdowns before at coastal plants in France, Sweden and Japan, usually in warm months when the creatures gather in huge numbers. The operator stressed that the shutdowns are a safety precaution rather than an emergency, and that the reactors will be brought back online once the intakes are cleaned. For France, where nuclear power supplies most of the country's electricity, the episode is a curiosity rather than a crisis — but it is also a small warning about the fragility of the energy systems Europe depends on as winter begins.

articles.title: Yandex Music will tell listeners when a track was made with AI
articles.description: Russian streaming service Yandex Music will now tell listeners when artificial intelligence was used in creating a track, Meduza reports. The move comes as AI-generated music floods streaming platforms and listeners increasingly cannot tell what is human-made. It matters because labelling is becoming the industry's main answer to the AI flood — and Russia's biggest streamer is adopting it too.
articles.body: The Russian streaming service Yandex Music will inform listeners when artificial intelligence was used in the creation of a track, Meduza reports. The labelling will appear on tracks where AI played a role in their production, giving users a signal they have not had before on the platform. The move comes as AI-generated music is flooding streaming services worldwide: tools like Suno can produce finished-sounding songs in seconds, and platforms are struggling with how much of their catalogue is now machine-made. For listeners, the labels answer a simple question — was this made by a person or a program — that has become surprisingly hard to answer by ear alone. For artists, labelling cuts both ways: it protects human creators from being crowded out by synthetic tracks, but it may also mark AI-assisted work as lesser. Yandex Music is Russia's largest streaming service, so its decision sets a standard for the Russian-language market, following similar labelling steps by global platforms. The change lands amid a wave of lawsuits against AI music companies, including the Elvis Presley rightsholders' case against Suno, and it shows the industry converging on transparency as its first response to the AI wave.

articles.title: Russia fires 3 ballistic missiles and 148 drones overnight; air defences down 117 as Kryvyi Rih toll rises
articles.description: Russia attacked Ukraine overnight into November 21 with 3 ballistic missiles and 148 attack drones, 87 of them jet-powered, Ukraine's air force reported; air defences shot down or suppressed 117 drones, with hits recorded at 19 locations. The heaviest blow fell on Kryvyi Rih, where the death toll stands at two and 58 people are injured. Drones also hit a five-storey building in Kharkiv region, injuring 11 people including two children, and struck an enterprise in Rivne region, starting a large fire.
articles.body: Russia launched a fresh overnight attack on Ukraine into November 21, firing 3 ballistic missiles and 148 attack drones, 87 of them jet-powered, according to Ukraine's air force. Air defences shot down or suppressed 117 of the drones, but hits were recorded at 19 locations across the country. The worst of the night was in Kryvyi Rih, where ballistic missiles struck the city centre on the evening of November 20: two people were killed, a 7-year-old boy and a 20-year-old paramedic, and 58 were injured, including six children, with a hospital, around 25 apartment blocks and ambulances damaged. In Kharkiv region, a drone hit a five-storey residential building, injuring 11 people including two children and starting a fire across apartments on the fourth and fifth floors. In Rivne region, a strike on an enterprise set off a large fire that emergency services extinguished during the night, and Russia's defence ministry claimed hits on the Kryvyi Rih thermal power plant and an electricity substation in Sarny. In Kyiv, the morning brought fires in two private houses in the Podil district after a Russian attack, and the city reported problems with water supply. The overnight barrage was smaller than the massive November 20 attack of around 100 missiles and 400 drones, but it shows Russia is sustaining nightly pressure on Ukrainian cities and energy infrastructure as winter approaches, and that air defences, while intercepting most drones, cannot stop every strike.

articles.title: Zelenskyy answers Musk on Starshield: 'Not everything is decided by money'
articles.description: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has answered Elon Musk, who said at the DealBook summit on November 18 that Zelenskyy 'doesn't always tell the truth' about problems with the Starshield military satellite system in Ukraine. In a CNN interview, Zelenskyy insisted the outages were 'one hundred percent true', said Ukraine has evidence of the communication failures, and noted the system was restored after his conversations with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio. The row matters because Starshield outages limited Ukrainian drone interceptions and frontline communications for a week.
articles.body: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has answered Elon Musk's accusation that he misrepresented problems with the Starshield military satellite system in Ukraine. Musk said at the DealBook summit on November 18 that Zelenskyy 'doesn't always tell the truth' about restrictions on Ukraine's access to Starshield, denied SpaceX's involvement, called Starlink a civilian system and said responsibility for Starshield's use in offensive operations lay with the US government and the Pentagon. In an interview with CNN, Zelenskyy pushed back: 'When I said Starshield wasn't working, it was one hundred percent true,' he said, adding that Ukraine has evidence of the communication failures and sees no reason to invent them. He said the system's work was restored after his conversations with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, though he does not know who exactly fixed it. 'And by the way, about the truth — that is for Elon. If he wants to find the one who doesn't tell the truth, he can call his friend,' Zelenskyy added, in an apparent reference to Musk's ties in Washington. The dispute is not academic: Zelenskyy had earlier reported that Starshield outages lasted a seventh straight day, with speeds on occupied territories capped at 161 km/h, hampering Ukrainian interception of Russian drones, reconnaissance and strikes, and he said the restrictions stopped 2,000 Ukrainian 'Bars' drones. The public spat lays bare how dependent Ukraine's military is on a single private company's satellite network — and on the politics of its owner.

articles.title: Zelenskyy tells NBC the Crimean Bridge 'will not survive' — during the war or after it
articles.description: In an interview with NBC News, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the Crimean Bridge will not survive — neither during the war nor after it ends — and called it a legitimate Ukrainian target. He explained the strikes on the bridge as a response to Russian attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure. The statement follows three Ukrainian strikes on the bridge in a week, on November 17, 18 and 19, which damaged both its road and rail sections.
articles.body: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said in an interview with NBC News that the Crimean Bridge will not survive — neither during the war nor after it is over. He called the bridge a legitimate target for Ukraine and explained the strikes on it as a response to Russian attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure. The statement follows a week in which Ukrainian forces hit the bridge three times: on November 17 and 18, Neptune and Ruta missiles collapsed a road span into the sea, and on November 19 they damaged the railway section, halting rail traffic between Russia and occupied Crimea. Ukrainian forces say the road section is 'dead' and no car will pass on it, and Crimea has arranged free ferry crossings across the Kerch Strait in place of the bridge. The bridge is both a symbol of Russian control over Crimea and a working military supply route, and Zelenskyy has repeatedly explained that destroying it serves both purposes at once. His NBC remark is the bluntest statement yet of Ukraine's intent: the bridge is not a target of opportunity but a structure Kyiv plans to finish. It also sets up a direct clash with Vladimir Putin, who said in Shenzhen on November 19 that Russia will not negotiate a ceasefire after the bridge strikes and threatened a 'much more painful' response. For the diplomacy around the war, Zelenskyy's words signal that Ukraine will keep striking Russian logistics even while peace talks are under way.

articles.title: Poland explains why it did not open fire on Russian air targets on November 20
articles.description: Poland's military command has explained why it did not shoot at Russian air targets during the massive November 20 attack on Ukraine, saying the necessary conditions for the use of weapons were not met. The explanation follows Warsaw's confirmation that two Russian missiles and a jet-powered drone fell on Polish soil that night. It matters because the decision not to fire has drawn questions in Poland and among allies about how NATO handles Russian incursions.
articles.body: Poland's military command has explained why Polish forces did not open fire on Russian air targets during the massive Russian attack on Ukraine on November 20, saying the necessary conditions for the use of weapons were not fulfilled. The statement comes a day after Warsaw confirmed that three Russian objects fell on Polish territory during the barrage: two missiles and a jet-powered drone, with a Kh-101 cruise missile landing in the village of Nowy Lipowiec, another missile in Rudnik nad Sanem and the drone in Mołodycz. Air raid alerts had sounded in two Polish provinces bordering Ukraine as the attack unfolded. The decision not to fire has drawn public attention in Poland and among NATO allies, since the alliance has scrambled jets in response to earlier Russian airspace violations and has debated how firmly to respond to repeated incursions without escalating into direct confrontation with Moscow. The command's explanation — that the engagement criteria were not met — suggests the objects were tracked but judged not to pose a threat justifying interception, or that they were already falling when identified. The incident remains one of the most serious airspace violations of the war, and the Polish explanation is likely to feed the ongoing debate in NATO about rules of engagement for Russian missiles and drones that cross allied borders.

articles.title: NABU and SAP uncover about 505 fraudulent call centres in 'Carthage' operation — and report obstruction of the investigation
articles.description: The heads of Ukraine's National Anti-Corruption Bureau (NABU) and Specialised Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office (SAP) have announced the discovery of around 505 fraudulent call centres in an operation codenamed 'Carthage', and reported obstacles to the investigation. The scale of the fraud network is striking: hundreds of call centres running scams, apparently with protection. It matters because the operation tests whether Ukraine's anti-corruption bodies can take on organised fraud at industrial scale.
articles.body: The heads of Ukraine's National Anti-Corruption Bureau (NABU) and the Specialised Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office (SAP) have said their 'Carthage' operation uncovered around 505 fraudulent call centres, and have reported obstacles to the investigation. The scale of the find is remarkable: hundreds of call centres operating as a coordinated fraud network, scamming victims — in Ukraine and abroad — out of money through deceptive calls. The announcement was among the lead domestic stories on the morning of November 21, Ukraine's Day of Dignity and Freedom, a day that itself commemorates the struggle for honest government. The reported obstruction of the investigation is the other half of the story: the anti-corruption chiefs say their work is being impeded, a familiar complaint for NABU and SAP, whose independence has been contested by political forces in Kyiv. The operation comes as Ukraine's partners, above all the European Union, condition further support on credible anti-corruption progress, and as the government faces pressure to show that wartime Ukraine is cleaning up the fraud and graft that have long plagued it. Whether 'Carthage' leads to prosecutions of the network's organisers, rather than just its low-level operators, will be the real test of the operation's significance.

articles.title: European Commission transfers €7.9 billion to Ukraine — the largest single Ukraine Facility tranche yet
articles.description: The European Commission has transferred €7.9 billion to Ukraine, the largest single tranche under the EU's Ukraine Facility programme. The money lands as the EU pledges €90 billion for Ukraine through the end of 2027 following the Coalition of the Willing meeting in Berlin. It matters because the funding gives Kyiv budget certainty for the winter while Russia keeps striking its energy grid.
articles.body: The European Commission has transferred €7.9 billion to Ukraine, the largest single tranche yet under the EU's Ukraine Facility programme, Ukrainian media reported on November 20. The payment is part of the EU's long-term support for Kyiv's budget and reconstruction, and it follows the Coalition of the Willing meeting in Berlin, where the EU pledged €90 billion for Ukraine through the end of 2027 and NATO partners committed €70 billion in military aid for 2026. The €7.9 billion tranche is the biggest single disbursement so far under the Facility, which was set up to give Ukraine predictable, multi-year funding rather than ad-hoc emergency aid. The money arrives at a critical moment: Russia has launched more than 1,000 strikes on Ukraine's energy system since September, emergency power outages are in force across the country, and the government needs budget support to keep the state running and the grid repaired through the winter. The transfer also signals that Brussels is moving ahead with funding regardless of the uncertainty in Washington, where President Trump has questioned further spending on military support for Ukraine. For Kyiv, the combination of the record tranche and the €90 billion pledge means it can plan its war effort and energy repairs into 2027 rather than living month to month.

articles.title: Frontline: 203 combat engagements in a day; Zaporizhzhia region hit by 489 strikes, two killed and 22 injured
articles.description: Ukraine's General Staff reported 203 combat engagements over the past day, with the heaviest fighting continuing on the eastern front. In Zaporizhzhia region, Russian forces carried out 489 strikes on 48 settlements in a single day, killing two people and injuring 22, including a child. A Russian missile also damaged the Pechenihy dam in Kharkiv region, closing the road across it.
articles.body: Ukraine's General Staff reported 203 combat engagements over the past day in its morning update on November 21, as Russian forces continued pressing on multiple axes. The figure is down from the 278 engagements reported on November 20 but still reflects intense fighting across the front, with the hottest sectors remaining around Pokrovsk, Dobropillia and Kostiantynivka in the east. In Zaporizhzhia region, the regional authorities reported that Russian forces carried out 489 strikes on 48 settlements over the course of November 20, killing two people and injuring 22, including one child, in attacks on the city of Zaporizhzhia and the surrounding district. In Kharkiv region, a Russian missile strike at around 1 AM damaged a section of the T-21-11 road at the Pechenihy dam, making passage across the dam impossible and forcing drivers onto a detour through Chuhuiv, Korobochkyne and Lebyazhe. The General Staff's evening update on November 20 had reported 157 combat engagements since the start of that day, with heavy use of drones on both sides. The frontline picture underlines that the diplomatic activity in Shenzhen and Berlin has not slowed the war on the ground: Russia is continuing offensive operations and strikes on civilian areas while simultaneously talking about peace, and Ukraine's forces are holding defensive lines under sustained pressure.

articles.title: Former Take-Two chief: GTA VI is the last hand-made blockbuster — AI will build the next ones
articles.description: Former Take-Two Interactive CEO Ben Feder says Grand Theft Auto VI marks the end of an era: in a column for Fortune, he calls Rockstar's crime epic the last fully hand-made blockbuster, arguing that generative AI is about to transform how games are built. Thousands of artists, programmers, writers and designers worked on GTA VI for around a decade, a model Feder says has stopped being profitable. It matters because the most successful game ever made may also be the last of its kind.
articles.body: Former Take-Two Interactive CEO Ben Feder believes the release of Grand Theft Auto VI closes a whole era in game development. In a column for Fortune, he called Rockstar's crime epic the last super-blockbuster created entirely by hand, predicting that studios will now lean ever harder on AI tools. For decades, he argues, there was only one way to make a game world bigger and richer: raise the budget and hire more people — and GTA VI took around ten years and thousands of artists, programmers, writers and designers. At that scale, abandoning even one failed idea is enormously expensive: Feder cites Red Dead Redemption 2, from which Rockstar cut around five hours late in development, including one of Arthur Morgan's love storylines, after the team had already spent time and money building it. He says many studios cannot even afford to rework mistakes, because they run out of time and funding and must ship what they have. Generative AI, in his view, lets a small team build a playable rough version of an episode early, test whether the idea works, and only then bring in the full team — or try something else without losing months or years. He compares the shift to the arrival of photography, which cost portrait painters work but pushed artists toward bolder experiments. His blunt conclusion: AAA development in its classic form has stopped being profitable, publishers do not know how to make games for less than $300 million, and games take so long to build that audience tastes move on before release — GTA VI is a rare exception, and the industry is entering a time of change.

articles.title: Insider: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic remake to be re-announced at The Game Awards
articles.description: Saber Interactive is planning to re-announce the long-troubled remake of Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic at The Game Awards on December 10, according to insider and YouTuber Luke Hull. The remake was first announced in 2021 and has gone almost completely silent since changing developers. A TGA reveal would confirm the project is still alive after years of doubt.
articles.body: The remake of Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic may finally resurface at The Game Awards 2026 on December 10. According to well-known YouTube insider Luke Hull, Saber Interactive plans to use the ceremony for a second announcement of the project, which has been shrouded in uncertainty for years. The remake was first revealed in 2021, originally in development at Aspyr, before reports of troubled production and a change of studio left fans wondering whether it still existed at all. Saber Interactive, which took over the project, has said almost nothing about it publicly since. A re-announcement on Geoff Keighley's stage — one of the biggest audiences in gaming — would be a strong signal that the game is genuinely back on track rather than quietly cancelled. Knights of the Old Republic, first released in 2003 by BioWare, remains one of the most beloved Star Wars games ever made, and a modern remake has been one of the community's longest-running wishes. For now the report is still a rumour, but if it holds, December 10 becomes one of the most anticipated nights of the year for Star Wars fans.

articles.title: Sony to remove at least six games from PS Plus Extra in December — including Granblue Fantasy: Relink
articles.description: Sony will remove at least six games from the PlayStation Plus Extra catalogue on December 15, GameMAG reports. The departures include the role-playing game Granblue Fantasy: Relink and the adventure Jake Hunter Detective Story: Prism of Eyes, plus a co-op action title. Subscribers have just under a month to finish them before they leave the service.
articles.body: PlayStation Plus Extra subscribers should check their backlogs: Sony is set to remove at least six games from the expanded subscription catalogue on December 15. Among the departures are the role-playing game Granblue Fantasy: Relink, the adventure Jake Hunter Detective Story: Prism of Eyes and a co-operative action game, with the full list still to be confirmed. The removals are part of Sony's regular monthly rotation, which drops older titles as new ones arrive — November's additions, including Death Stranding 2, Atomfall and Dragon Quest III HD-2D Remake, only went live this week. For players partway through Granblue Fantasy: Relink, a substantial RPG, the deadline is a real one: progress made in the subscription version will not carry over unless the game is bought outright. The December cull lands right in the middle of the holiday season, when many players finally have time to catch up on their libraries. Sony typically announces the outgoing titles a few weeks ahead, giving subscribers a final window to play them before they disappear from the catalogue.

articles.title: Persona 6 won't end the series — Atlus plans to release sequels faster
articles.description: Atlus has no plans to end the Persona series with Persona 6, P-Studio general producer Kazuhisa Wada has confirmed. Instead, the team is changing how it works so fans will not have to wait around ten years between numbered entries, as they did between Persona 5 and Persona 6. It is the clearest sign yet that Persona is now a permanent flagship franchise for Atlus.
articles.body: Persona 6 will not be the end of Atlus's beloved JRPG series. P-Studio general producer Kazuhisa Wada has confirmed that the team does not plan to wrap up Persona after the sixth numbered entry, and is instead changing its development approach so that sequels arrive faster. Fans waited roughly a decade between Persona 5 and the next mainline game, a gap Wada says the studio wants to avoid repeating. The shift reflects how central Persona has become to Atlus: what began as a spin-off of Shin Megami Tensei is now one of the publisher's biggest franchises, with Persona 5 alone selling millions of copies and spawning anime, stage shows and spin-off games. Speeding up production without sacrificing quality is a familiar challenge for Japanese RPG studios, and Wada's comments suggest Atlus is reorganising its teams and pipelines to make it possible. No release date or platform details for Persona 6 itself have been announced yet. But the message to fans is clear: the series has a long future, and the waits between entries should get shorter.

articles.title: AI trailer backlash forces Shift Up to rethink AI use after Stellar Blade: Blood Rain video
articles.description: South Korean studio Shift Up has changed its approach to artificial intelligence after players reacted angrily to a music trailer for Stellar Blade: Blood Rain that was made with AI. Many Stellar Blade fans criticised the video, and the studio has now reconsidered how it uses neural networks in its marketing. The episode shows how sensitive the AI question has become even for studios with a loyal fanbase.
articles.body: Shift Up, the South Korean studio behind Stellar Blade, has revised its approach to artificial intelligence after a backlash over an AI-made music trailer for Stellar Blade: Blood Rain. Many fans criticised the video for being generated with neural networks, arguing that a studio known for its hand-crafted character art should not cut corners with AI-generated marketing. The reaction was sharp enough that Shift Up has now publicly reconsidered how it uses AI, a rare climbdown in an industry where publishers are increasingly open about adopting generative tools. The controversy lands in the middle of a wider debate in gaming: players have pushed back against AI-generated art, voice work and trailers across several major releases this year, while developers argue the tools can speed up routine work. For Shift Up, the stakes are particularly high — Stellar Blade's visual identity and its fan community are core to the game's success, and alienating that audience over a trailer is a costly mistake. The studio has not detailed exactly what its new policy will be, but the signal is clear: for now, AI-generated promotional material is off the table, or at least heavily reconsidered.

articles.title: New Call of Duty fails to crack the US top 10 bestsellers of 2026, Circana reports
articles.description: The new Call of Duty has failed to make the top 10 best-selling games of 2026 in the United States, according to Circana's October sales report — a striking stumble for a franchise that has topped the charts almost every year. Previous entries, including Black Ops 6 and Black Ops 7, launched far stronger. It is the latest sign that the once-unstoppable formula is losing its grip.
articles.body: Call of Duty's grip on the American sales charts is slipping. According to Circana's report on US game and console sales for October 2026, the new Call of Duty failed to break into the ten best-selling games of the year in the United States — a remarkable result for a series that has dominated the annual charts for well over a decade. Earlier entries in the franchise launched considerably stronger, and the report notes that both Black Ops 6 and Black Ops 7 got off to better starts. The miss comes in a year when the charts have been reshaped by GTA VI's record-breaking launch and a crowded autumn release calendar, but Call of Duty has historically sold through any competition. Analysts will be watching whether the weak showing reflects franchise fatigue, a crowded market, or the specific reception of this year's entry, which has drawn mixed reactions from players. For Activision, the numbers are a warning: the formula that carried the series for years — an annual release, a big multiplayer launch and a steady stream of seasonal content — is no longer a guarantee of a top-ten finish. The full-year charts will show whether the game recovers over the holiday season or whether 2026 becomes the year Call of Duty lost its crown.

articles.title: Rockstar reveals GTA VI's lead actors: Dylan Rourke plays Jason Duval, Manny L. Perez is Lucia Caminos
articles.description: Rockstar Games has finally revealed who plays Grand Theft Auto VI's two protagonists: the release-day credits list Dylan Rourke as Jason Duval and Manny L. Perez as Lucia Caminos. Fans had suspected both names for months, but Rockstar kept the cast secret until launch day. It is the first time the actors have spoken publicly about working on the biggest game ever made.
articles.body: Rockstar Games has revealed the actors behind Grand Theft Auto VI's two leads. The credits published on release day list Dylan Rourke as Jason Duval and Manny L. Perez as Lucia Caminos, the criminal couple at the centre of the game's story in the fictional state of Leonida. Fans had long suspected both names — Rourke in particular had been linked to the role by casting rumours — but Rockstar kept the cast under wraps until the game was in players' hands, in keeping with the secrecy around the whole project. The actors have now begun speaking for the first time about working on the game, describing the experience of performing in a production that spanned years and employed thousands of people. Rourke's Jason and Perez's Lucia are the first dual protagonists of a mainline GTA since GTA V's trio, and their relationship is the emotional core of the story. The reveal also ends years of speculation and fan detective work, which included analysing trailers frame by frame for clues about the cast. With the game now out and breaking every sales record, its stars can finally step into the spotlight.

articles.title: Trump defends calling Putin a 'friend', floats a Stephen Miller presidential run and vows a data-centre tax
articles.description: President Donald Trump made a high-profile White House briefing-room appearance on Friday after returning from a four-day trip to Asia, defending his close personal friendships with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin even as their conversations brought him no closer to ending Russia's war on Ukraine. He floated his new chief of staff Stephen Miller as a possible 2028 presidential candidate, announced a planned tax crackdown on US companies building data centres abroad, and doubled down on the Iran war. It was a wide-ranging appearance that mixed foreign policy, the 2028 shadow primary and his final two years in office.
articles.body: President Donald Trump returned to the White House briefing room on Friday after a four-day trip to Asia, in an appearance shaped by a pileup of domestic challenges — a string of sudden tech outages, rising AI worries and a looming confrontation with the new Democratic majorities in Congress. But first, Trump wanted to talk about his friendships with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin. 'We have a very great relationship,' he said, defending on multiple occasions calling Putin a 'friend', even as their regular conversations have brought him no closer to ending Russia's war on Ukraine. He expressed surprise at how difficult peace has been to broker, blaming the 'tremendous hatred' between Putin and Volodymyr Zelenskyy, and said his friendship with Putin is rooted in part in the fact they found themselves on the same side during his first-term impeachment over withholding aid to Ukraine. The briefing also offered a striking visual of the 2028 shadow primary: Vice President JD Vance over Trump's right shoulder and Secretary of State Marco Rubio to his left, while Trump turned to his new chief of staff Stephen Miller and called him 'the most powerful man in the room right now' before asking, 'Do you want to run for president?' On policy, Trump announced a planned crackdown on US companies building data centres outside the country, vowing a 'tremendous tax' on firms that offshore the structures powering the AI boom. He openly acknowledged the Iran war had soured Americans' mood and cost his party politically, but showed no sign of backing off a fight he insists was necessary to stop Iran obtaining a nuclear weapon. And pressed on his final two years, he said he would work with Democrats — while keeping the veto pen ready.

articles.title: DOJ Alaska investigation shifts focus to Peltola's campaign and Democratic operatives
articles.description: With Alaska's Senate race now called for Mary Peltola, the Justice Department's criminal investigation into an alleged spoiler-candidate scheme has shifted focus toward Peltola's own campaign, the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee and outside political consultants, CNN reports. The probe thrust the DOJ into the centre of a contentious race, and the department has sent dozens of FBI agents to Alaska and issued hundreds of subpoenas and preservation letters. It has also moved to drop its lawsuit seeking to block certification of Peltola's victory.
articles.body: The Justice Department's criminal investigation into Alaska's Senate race has taken a sharp turn now that the contest is decided. With the race called for Senator-elect Mary Peltola, who ousted incumbent Dan Sullivan, the investigation is shifting focus toward Peltola's campaign as part of its probe into an alleged scheme to run a spoiler candidate against her opponent, according to two people familiar with the matter. The focus has moved away from Sullivan and now centres on Peltola's campaign, the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee and outside political consultants allegedly involved in the scheme, another person familiar with the matter said. The investigation thrust the Justice Department into the centre of a contentious political race, and its scale is striking: the department has sent dozens of FBI agents to Alaska and issued hundreds of subpoenas and preservation letters as part of the probe. Gerald Heikes, a longshot candidate, was previously issued a subpoena, CNN reported. Meanwhile, the Justice Department has moved to drop its lawsuit seeking to block certification of Peltola's victory, a step that effectively accepts the result even as the criminal investigation continues. The shift raises fresh questions about how the department handles investigations touching on election campaigns, and it puts the winning campaign under the same scrutiny once aimed at its opponent.

articles.title: The Democrats' top 9 targets for investigations in the next Congress
articles.description: Democrats will soon take over both the House and the Senate, and CNN has ranked the nine investigations that make the most practical and political sense for them to pursue. The list runs from self-enrichment by Trump, his family and their allies at No. 1, through the Iran war, the Epstein files, ICE deportations, Nvidia and the Jensen Huang affair, the DOJ's legal retribution campaign, Elon Musk, Trump's renovations and the military boat strikes. A Pew poll this week found 67% of Americans worry Democrats will investigate 'too much' — so the party will have to choose its targets carefully.
articles.body: Democrats are about to take control of both chambers of Congress, and the question is no longer whether they will investigate the Trump administration, but what they will investigate first. CNN has ranked the nine targets that seem to make the most practical and political sense. At No. 1 is self-enrichment by Trump, his family and their allies; No. 2 is the Iran war, where CNN has reported Trump appeared to exaggerate how imminent the threat was, the strike relied on outdated intelligence, and a recent UN report found it might have been a war crime. No. 3 is the Epstein files, No. 4 is ICE and deportations, and No. 5 is Jensen Huang, Nvidia and the Megaspeed affair. Rounding out the list are the Justice Department's legal retribution campaign at No. 6, Elon Musk at No. 7 — including questions about whether Musk or the administration was responsible for Starlink being throttled and hampering Ukraine's war defence — Trump's renovations at No. 8, and the military boat strikes at No. 9, including the September 19 strike on an alleged drug-trafficking boat in the Caribbean. The political risk is real: a Pew Research Center poll this week showed 67% of Americans are more worried congressional Democrats will investigate 'too much', against 31% who fear 'not enough'. The ranking matters because Democrats have already begun laying the groundwork with document-preservation letters across the government, and the first hearings of the new Congress will set the tone for the next two years.

articles.title: Bukele promised Haiti a 'triumph'. Are his forces delivering?
articles.description: Thousands of Salvadoran troops landed in Haiti last month to combat the gangs overrunning the Caribbean nation, and it is too early to tell whether they are succeeding — but the personal involvement of El Salvador's popular President Nayib Bukele has stirred rare hope on the island and avid interest across Latin America. Haitian police announced on Thursday they had killed 34 gang members in a major operation in the Port-au-Prince neighbourhood of Martissant, and a secretive task force involving a private military contractor led by Erik Prince has been busy too. On Friday, two Salvadoran soldiers died and two were wounded in an incident handling explosive material.
articles.body: Thousands of Salvadoran troops landed in Haiti last month to combat the gangs that have overrun the Caribbean nation, and CNN reports it is too early to tell whether they are succeeding. What is clear is that the personal involvement of El Salvador's popular President Nayib Bukele has stirred rare hope on the island — and avid interest across Latin America, where leaders are watching whether his hardline security model can be exported. Haitian police, a secretive task force involving a private military contractor led by Erik Prince, and the multinational Gang Suppression Force have all been active: police announced on Thursday that they had killed 34 gang members in a major operation in the Port-au-Prince neighbourhood of Martissant. But the mission is already taking casualties. On Friday, two Salvadoran soldiers died and two others were wounded in an incident while handling explosive material, according to the Salvadoran army. The deployment is one of the most ambitious attempts yet to stabilise Haiti, where gangs control much of the capital and the state has struggled to reassert authority for years. Bukele built his reputation at home by crushing El Salvador's gangs with mass arrests and a state of emergency, a model admired by some leaders and condemned by human rights groups. Whether it can work in Haiti — a different country, with different gangs, and under a multinational mandate — is the question the whole region is now asking.

articles.title: A capsizing cruise ship and a gutsy risk: how a police chief turned a looming tragedy into a miracle in New Orleans
articles.description: When a hulking tanker lost control on the Mississippi River and crashed into a docked river cruise boat carrying 190 people, New Orleans Harbor Police Chief Melanie Montroll had just sat down at a Thanksgiving potluck — and never took a bite. In the two-minute drive to the scene, she prepared for the worst. Her officers got about 80 people off via the gangway while it was still attached, and in the end nobody among the 190 passengers and crew died, though 32 people were taken to hospital.
articles.body: New Orleans Harbor Police Chief Melanie Montroll had just grabbed a plate of food at the department's Thanksgiving potluck last Friday afternoon when the call came in — and, as she told CNN, she never got to take a bite. An Atlantic Asphalt tanker, a hulking industrial ship, had lost control as it made its way up the Mississippi River and crashed into a docked river cruise boat, the American Heritage, with 190 people on board. The riverboat capsized after the collision, and Montroll and her colleagues had carved only 45 minutes out of their schedules for the annual tradition before everything became all hands on deck. In the two-minute drive from the police station to the scene, sirens blaring, Montroll mentally prepared herself for what she might find. First responders managed to get about 80 people off the boat while the gangway was still attached to the dock, before it gave way. Thirty-two people were taken to hospital on Friday, including two officers who ran onto the riverboat as it was going over. None of the 190 passengers and crew died — a small miracle, officials said, in the face of what could have been a mass-casualty disaster on the river. The collision happened on November 13 near the Port of New Orleans, and the story of the rescue has become a rare moment of good news in a heavy week.

articles.title: The next big travel nightmare could start at the TSA check-in line
articles.description: The next travel nightmare may have nothing to do with technology outages and everything to do with political gridlock: funding for the federal government, including the TSA and the FAA, is set to expire on December 12. The Trump administration hopes to pass another stopgap funding bill, but the fight is effectively frozen until the Senate Democrats' internal leadership election on December 1. If a shutdown leaves airports short of TSA screeners and air traffic controllers, holiday travellers could face long lines and delays.
articles.body: The next travel nightmare could have nothing to do with technology outages and everything to do with political gridlock. Funding for the federal government — including the Transportation Security Administration and the Federal Aviation Administration — is set to expire on December 12, and a shutdown would leave airports short of the screeners and air traffic controllers who keep the system moving. The Trump administration hopes to avert a shutdown, and the preferred scenario among party leaders is to pass another stopgap funding bill, sources familiar with the plans told CNN. But the funding fight is effectively frozen until the Senate Democrats' internal leadership election on December 1, multiple lawmakers and senior aides in both parties told CNN, and then it will likely take weeks to reach an agreement. The warning lands just days after the FAA's nationwide ground stop on November 13, which stranded passengers across the country and showed how quickly the system can seize up. This time the risk is different: not a technical failure, but a political one, arriving right as the Thanksgiving and Christmas travel season peaks. For passengers, the practical advice is familiar — arrive early, expect lines — but the underlying problem is one only Congress can fix.

articles.title: What we know about the Army's planned detonation in Iowa after a judge ordered a temporary pause
articles.description: UPDATE: Residents in southeastern Iowa are still awaiting a decision on whether the US Army will detonate five tons of lead azide at a munitions plant, after a federal judge in the Eighth Circuit ordered a temporary pause on Thursday. The detonation of nearly 70 drums of the unstable explosive at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown was originally scheduled for Friday, then moved to Monday after public outcry. New details: the EPA emergency permit runs from November 13, 2026 to February 11, 2027, and forecast winds of 5–10 mph from the north could carry lead dust south over rural Iowa, the Mississippi River and into western Illinois.
articles.body: UPDATE — new details on a story covered in yesterday's digest: residents in southeastern Iowa are awaiting a decision on whether the US Army will detonate five tons of lead azide at a munitions plant, after a federal judge ordered a temporary pause. A judge in the Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals on Thursday ordered the Army to pause its plan to detonate the material at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, following a suit brought by environmental groups. The Army, in coordination with the US Environmental Protection Agency, plans to destroy nearly 70 drums of lead azide, a compound used to detonate munitions, which the military says has become unstable and dangerous to move — a risk that increases in cold weather. The detonation was originally scheduled for Friday morning, then rescheduled to Monday after pushback from the public and elected officials, with Monday described as the latest possible moment before a forecasted temperature drop. The emergency permit from the EPA, which went into effect on November 13, 2026 and runs through February 11, 2027, allows the Army to carry out the detonation in that window. The plans have drawn heavy pushback from Iowans, environmental advocates and politicians who worry about the plume, which could spread toxic lead dust over vast swaths of rural Iowa and the Mississippi River and potentially into part of western Illinois. Forecast winds blowing from north to south at around 5 to 10 mph could determine how far lead particles travel, according to CNN meteorologist Chris Dolce. A public advisory on Sunday was the first time some communities as far as 100 miles away learned of the potential impact, and residents near the plant told CNN they plan to evacuate when the detonation eventually goes ahead.

articles.title: Duetti secures $665M, led by a $450M Carlyle-anchored securitization, taking its funding past $1.3B
articles.description: Duetti has raised $665 million to buy more independent music catalogues, led by a $450 million asset-backed securitization anchored by Carlyle. The deal, announced November 17, takes Duetti's total funding past $1.3 billion since its 2022 founding. It is the company's third securitization in two years and more than five times its first.
articles.body: Duetti has secured $665 million to fund further investment in independent music catalogues, the company announced on November 17. The package includes a $450 million asset-backed securitization anchored by investment firm Carlyle, plus $165 million of additional credit capacity from Viola Credit and a $50 million side facility with Flexpoint Ford and Truist Bank. It is Duetti's third securitization in two years and more than five times the size of its inaugural $80 million deal in 2024, taking its total raised since its 2022 founding past $1.3 billion. Duetti says it has completed more than 1,600 catalogue investments since 2022 and now owns over 50,000 masters and compositions representing more than 3,000 recording artists from over 50 countries, describing itself as the world's most active catalogue company. Barclays co-led the latest deal alongside Truist, and the transaction achieved a ratings upgrade with a broader group of institutional investors than Duetti's prior issues. Carlyle, which also backs Litmus Music, has deployed more than $17 billion into sports, media and entertainment since 2017. The deal lands as rating agency KBRA forecasts music securitization issuance will fall about 25% in 2026, making Duetti's record raise a notable exception.

articles.title: Spotify's 'Marketplace' now costs the music industry over $700M a year — and could hit $1.9B by 2030
articles.description: Spotify's 'Marketplace' promotional tools now cost the music industry more than $700 million a year, according to a Music Business Worldwide analysis by founder Tim Ingham. Discovery Mode and tools like Marquee and Showcase generated about €640 million in gross profit for Spotify in 2025, and Ingham projects that could reach $1.9 billion a year by 2030. The analysis lands as Spotify renegotiates licences with Universal and Warner.
articles.body: Music Business Worldwide founder Tim Ingham calculates that labels, distributors and artists now sacrifice more than $700 million a year on Spotify's 'Marketplace' promotional tools, including Discovery Mode, and the figure could reach $1.9 billion a year by 2030. Discovery Mode, launched in 2020, lets artists and labels accept a lower royalty rate in exchange for algorithmic promotion, with Spotify taking a 30% commission on the royalties those tracks generate in contexts such as Radio and Autoplay. Spotify's Marketplace gross profit grew fourfold between 2021 and 2025, to around €640 million (roughly $720 million) — more than 30 times what it made in 2018 — and was worth about 12% of Spotify's total gross profit. Spotify is targeting a gross margin of 35%–40% by 2030, up from 32% in 2025, and CFO Christian Luiga named Marketplace the first driver that would get it there, calling it 'a fantastic lever for margin'. Ingham's projection assumes Marketplace holds its 3.7% share of Spotify revenue as revenues grow to €33–36 billion by 2030, yielding up to €1.7 billion. The analysis lands as Spotify negotiates licence renewals with Universal and Warner, whose current deals reach their two-year mark in early 2027.

articles.title: Vevo names its first DSCVR Artists to Watch for 2027: Dalvin La Melodía, Conep, Devon Again, Mari Froes and Die Spitz
articles.description: Vevo has named the first five acts on its DSCVR Artists to Watch 2027 list: bachata singer Dalvin La Melodía, Puerto Rican rapper Conep, pop experimentalist Devon Again, Brazilian singer-songwriter Mari Froes and Austin rock band Die Spitz. Devon Again recently opened for Olivia Rodrigo, and Die Spitz have supported Foo Fighters and King Gizzard. More artists will be revealed in the coming weeks.
articles.body: Vevo has unveiled the first batch of its DSCVR Artists to Watch 2027 list, in partnership with Music Business Worldwide, spotlighting five acts tipped to break out next year. Bachata singer Dalvin La Melodía, whose debut album is La Bachata Volvió, is the first bachata artist ever featured on a Vevo DSCVR set and is already setting attendance records on his debut tour, according to Vevo's Latin programming team. Puerto Rican rapper Conep broke through via the Freestyle Mania talent competition and earned a co-sign from Young Miko on the remix of 'After'. Pop experimentalist Devon Again was tapped by Olivia Rodrigo to open select dates of her sold-out North American Unraveled Tour. Brazilian singer-songwriter Mari Froes blends bossa nova, samba, jazz and alt-pop, while Austin four-piece Die Spitz move between grunge, punk and rock on their debut album Something to Consume and have opened for Foo Fighters, King Gizzard and Olivia Rodrigo. Each artist will be featured on MBW over the coming weeks with exclusive video content. The DSCVR list is one of the industry's most watched annual tips sheets for emerging talent.

articles.title: Ex-Hipgnosis exec Alexander Bonavia launches electronic label Rendezvous Sound with Create Music Group
articles.description: Former Hipgnosis and Warner executive Alexander Bonavia has launched Rendezvous Sound, a London electronic music label and publisher, in joint ventures with Create Music Group-backed broke Records and Enhanced Music. The company, launched November 19, says it already averages 100 million streams a month. Its publishing catalogue includes hits from Dom Dolla, Tiësto, Meduza and Odesza.
articles.body: Former Warner Music Group and Hipgnosis executive Alexander Bonavia has launched Rendezvous Sound, a London-based electronic music label and publishing company, officially unveiled on November 19. The label operates as a joint venture with broke Records, while its publishing division has partnered with Will Holland's Enhanced Music; Create Music Group owns broke and acquired a 50% stake in Enhanced in December 2024. Rendezvous Sound says its label already averages 100 million streams a month, with successes including Kolter's 'Trapped', which peaked at No. 48 on the UK Official Singles Chart and was B-listed by BBC Radio 1, and Joshwa's 'Out of My Mind', which has generated 30 million streams. The publishing division's catalogue includes hits from Prospa, Rampa, Dom Dolla, Tiësto, Meduza, Blond:ish, Moby and Odesza, and it claims syncs including three songs in the upcoming blockbuster Children of Blood and Bone plus deals with MrBeast, NBA 2K and GTA 6. Bonavia was previously SVP of Creative at Hipgnosis, where he says he built a business generating 4 billion streams a year, and VP of Global Marketing at Warner, working on campaigns for Fred again.., Tiësto, David Guetta, Dua Lipa and Coldplay.

articles.title: Felipe Holguin named CEO of Universal Music Latin America & Iberian Peninsula
articles.description: Universal Music Group has named Felipe Holguin as CEO of Universal Music Latin America & Iberian Peninsula, effective immediately. He succeeds Jesús López, who led UMG's Latin business for over 25 years and becomes Chairman Emeritus of Global Talent Services. Holguin previously ran Fusion Media Group at Univision and most recently worked with HYBE Latin America.
articles.body: Universal Music Group has appointed Felipe Holguin as CEO of Universal Music Latin America & Iberian Peninsula, effective immediately, the company announced on November 17. Holguin succeeds Jesús López, who led UMG's Latin music business for more than 25 years and moves to a new role as Chairman Emeritus of Global Talent Services, the artist management company he conceived. Holguin will report to UMG chairman and CEO Sir Lucian Grainge and lead UMG's Latin operations across the US, Latin America and Iberia, working to identify and develop the next generation of talent. He is described by UMG as a versatile executive and entrepreneur with more than 30 years of experience across music, media, technology and finance. His previous roles include CEO of Fusion Media Group at Univision, where he grew its English-language division to 92 million monthly unique visitors, and executive vice president of digital, news and music at Univision. Most recently he worked with HYBE Latin America on strategy and operations. The appointment comes as Latin America remains the fastest-growing recorded music region in the world, with revenues up 17.1% in 2025 according to IFPI, its 16th consecutive year of growth.

articles.title: Patrick Stewart's cause of death revealed: cardiopulmonary arrest, Alzheimer's and Lewy body dementia
articles.description: Patrick Stewart's cause of death has been revealed, Rolling Stone reported: his death certificate lists cardiopulmonary arrest and a neurocognitive disorder with Lewy body, with Alzheimer's disease also a factor. The Star Trek and X-Men actor died on October 28 at 86, at his Los Angeles home. His remains were handled by water cremation on November 3.
articles.body: Sir Patrick Stewart's official cause of death has been revealed, nearly a month after the Star Trek and X-Men actor died at 86. His death certificate, obtained by TMZ and released by the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner on November 19, lists cardiopulmonary arrest and a neurocognitive disorder with Lewy body as the causes of death, with Alzheimer's disease also a factor. Stewart died on October 28 at his Los Angeles home, in the care of his wife Sunny, following what his family described as 'a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia'. The certificate also revealed that his remains were handled through alkaline hydrolysis — water cremation — on November 3, a process that uses water and alkaline chemicals instead of flames. Stewart had not publicly disclosed his diagnoses, and his death shocked fans who had seen him promoting his return as Professor X in the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday. Tributes poured in from co-stars including Ian McKellen, William Shatner, Hugh Jackman and Judi Dench. Lewy body dementia is the second most common type of dementia after Alzheimer's, affecting memory, thinking and movement.

articles.title: Man found guilty of igniting the blaze that became the devastating Palisades Fire
articles.description: A federal jury has found Jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, guilty of starting the fire that became the devastating Palisades Fire, Rolling Stone reported. The retrial verdict came on November 20, five months after his first trial ended in a hung jury. The January 2025 fire killed 12 people and destroyed more than 6,800 structures; he faces 5 to 40 years in prison.
articles.body: A federal jury has found Jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, guilty of starting the blaze that grew into the devastating Palisades Fire, Rolling Stone reported. Five months after jurors deadlocked in his first trial, a second jury convicted him on Friday, November 20, of destruction of property by means of fire and arson affecting interstate commerce. Prosecutors said Rinderknecht, a former Uber driver and onetime Pacific Palisades resident, deliberately lit a brush fire with a lighter in the early hours of New Year's Day 2025. The blaze, known as the Lachman fire, was contained by firefighters but continued to smoulder underground, and six days later Santa Ana winds reignited it into the Palisades Fire, which burned for 24 days. The fire killed 12 people, scorched 23,448 acres across Pacific Palisades, Topanga and Malibu, destroyed 6,837 structures and forced 30,000 people to flee. Rinderknecht, who has been in custody since his arrest in Florida in October 2025, declined to testify at either trial and maintains his innocence, with his defence arguing fireworks caused the blaze. He faces a minimum of five years and a maximum of 40 years in prison, with sentencing set for March 17, 2027.

articles.title: Home Alone' sequel in the works with Macaulay Culkin returning as a grown-up Kevin
articles.description: A new Home Alone sequel is in the works at Disney with Macaulay Culkin returning as Kevin McCallister, Rolling Stone reported. Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg will write and produce, working from Culkin's own idea: a grown-up Kevin, now a father, locked out of his own house. It would be Culkin's first Home Alone film since 1992 — 34 years ago.
articles.body: A new Home Alone sequel is in development at Disney's 20th Century Studios with Macaulay Culkin returning as Kevin McCallister, Rolling Stone reported, citing Puck and Deadline. Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg have closed a deal to produce through their Point Grey banner and are working with Culkin on the screenplay, based on the actor's own idea. Culkin pitched Disney film chief David Greenbaum over the summer on a story following an older Kevin who is now a father — reportedly a widower or divorcee raising a child alone, who becomes locked out of his own house and must break back in past his son's traps. It would be Culkin's first Home Alone film since 1992's Home Alone 2: Lost in New York, 34 years ago, and his first live-action film role in years — he has acted in only one live-action film in the last decade. The franchise continued without him through a 1997 third film, two made-for-TV sequels and 2021's Home Sweet Home Alone. Culkin, now a father of two young sons, recently played a grown-up Kevin in McDonald's holiday ads, and the 1990 original is back in the Nielsen streaming top 10 with 177 million minutes viewed on Disney+. Disney has not officially confirmed the project, and Rogen and Goldberg have a horror comedy to direct for Universal first.

articles.title: Rosalía calls Taylor Swift a 'master songwriter' and names 'Wildest Dreams' as her favourite Swift song
articles.description: Rosalía has called Taylor Swift a 'master songwriter' in a red-carpet interview at the LOS40 Music Awards in Barcelona, Rolling Stone reported. She named 'Wildest Dreams' as her favourite Swift song, saying it is one of the songs she has listened to most in her entire life. The praise returns Swift's own compliment: she recently called Rosalía's album LUX 'perfect'.
articles.body: Rosalía has called Taylor Swift a 'master songwriter', speaking on the red carpet at the LOS40 Music Awards in Barcelona on November 20, Rolling Stone reported. 'To me, she's a master, honestly,' the Spanish singer said. 'I think she's incredible.' Asked about her favourite Swift song, Rosalía said she prefers individual songs to whole albums and named 'Wildest Dreams', the 2014 single from Swift's album 1989, as one of the songs she has listened to most in her entire life. The praise was a return volley: earlier in November, Swift had called Rosalía's album LUX a 'perfect album' and named it among the records that defined her year. The mutual admiration comes as both singers head to the 2027 Grammy Awards as rivals, with LUX and Swift's The Life of a Showgirl both nominated for Album of the Year, and their songs 'Berghain' and 'The Fate of Ophelia' competing for Record of the Year. Rosalía's comments were among the most-shared pop moments of the night, a rare public exchange of praise between two of the biggest names in pop.

articles.title: Bowen Yang apologizes for calling Regina Spektor an antisemitic slur on his podcast
articles.description: Bowen Yang has apologized for using an antisemitic slur to describe singer Regina Spektor on his Las Culturistas podcast. In an Instagram statement on November 20, the former Saturday Night Live star said he used the word 'Zio' without knowing its antisemitic history. The term, popularized by ex-Ku Klux Klan leader David Duke, surfaced in a clip from the October 14 episode.
articles.body: Bowen Yang has apologized after facing backlash for using an antisemitic slur to describe singer Regina Spektor on his Las Culturistas podcast, Rolling Stone reported. In a statement posted to Instagram on Friday, November 20, the Saturday Night Live alum said: 'I want to genuinely apologize for using a word on the podcast without knowing its antisemitic history, especially since we've repudiated antisemitism on the show as recently as the last two weeks.' He added it was 'particularly upsetting to realize that I adopted language popularized by far-right movements whose rhetoric we should be wary of and act against.' The remark came in a resurfaced clip from the October 14 episode, in which guest Edy Modica called Spektor 'a little Israel hardcore' and Yang replied, 'Yeah, she's Zio' — 'Zio' being a term popularized by former Ku Klux Klan leader David Duke and classified by the American Jewish Committee as an antisemitic slur. The clip drew criticism from figures including Jewish Council for Public Affairs CEO Amy Spitalnick. Yang, who left SNL in 2025 after seven seasons, followed the apology with a separate Instagram Story message reading 'At the same time. Free Palestine.'

articles.title: BLACKPINK's Jisoo debuts buoyant single 'Sun Showers' for The Angry Birds Movie 3
articles.description: BLACKPINK's Jisoo has released 'Sun Showers', a buoyant new solo single recorded for The Angry Birds Movie 3, Rolling Stone reported. The track, co-written by Jisoo, arrived on Friday, November 20, with a video featuring scenes from the film, which opens December 23. It continues her solo run ahead of her anticipated debut album.
articles.body: BLACKPINK's Jisoo has released her buoyant new solo single 'Sun Showers', recorded and co-written for Paramount Pictures' The Angry Birds Movie 3, Rolling Stone reported. The feel-good pop track arrived on Friday, November 20, alongside an official music video featuring scenes from the film, which opens in cinemas on December 23. The song will appear in the film itself as well as in promotional trailers. The single continues Jisoo's solo run ahead of her anticipated debut solo album, following recent standalone releases including 'Click' and 'Addicted', with the full-length project teased throughout 2026. The cover art and visuals feature Shumon, a small dustball-inspired creature Jisoo originally drew in middle school. Directed by John Rice, The Angry Birds Movie 3 follows Red as he faces fatherhood and saving the world. Jisoo's bandmates have also kept busy with solo work, and the BLACKPINK members' individual releases have become one of the defining K-pop stories of the year.

articles.title: Blondie return with wistful new song 'Come Back Home' featuring Lucius
articles.description: Blondie have released a wistful new song, 'Come Back Home', featuring harmony duo Lucius, Rolling Stone reported. The track pairs the veteran New York band with one of indie-pop's most in-demand vocal acts. It is Blondie's latest new music, arriving in a busy week of releases.
articles.body: Blondie have released a new song, 'Come Back Home', featuring Lucius, Rolling Stone reported on November 19. The wistful track finds the veteran New York band in reflective mood, with the harmonies of Lucius — the duo of Jess Wolfe and Holly Laessig — woven through the song. It is the band's latest new music and a reminder of Blondie's continuing creative life nearly five decades after they first emerged from the New York punk scene. The collaboration pairs one of the most influential bands of the late 1970s with a younger harmony-driven act known for working with artists across indie and pop. Lucius have become sought-after collaborators in recent years, lending their voices to a string of high-profile records. 'Come Back Home' arrived as part of a busy week of new music that also saw releases from Jisoo, Burna Boy, Gracie Abrams and Lisa. For longtime fans, the song is a welcome return from a band that has kept recording and touring while its early catalogue continues to find new audiences.

articles.title: P!NK extends her Las Vegas Sphere residency into 2028, adding six January shows
articles.description: P!NK is extending her Las Vegas Sphere residency into 2028, adding six shows on January 19, 21, 22, 26, 28 and 29, 2028, Billboard reported. The additions follow three extra November 2027 dates and take the residency to 18 shows — double the nine originally announced. She will be the first solo female pop artist to headline Sphere when the run opens on September 29, 2027.
articles.body: P!NK is extending her forthcoming Las Vegas residency at Sphere into 2028, adding six performances on January 19, 21, 22, 26, 28 and 29, 2028, Billboard reported. The new dates follow three extra November 2027 shows, taking the residency to 18 performances in total — double the nine originally announced on November 9. The run opens on September 29, 2027, and will make P!NK the first solo female pop artist to headline Sphere, the immersive Las Vegas venue wrapped in the world's highest-resolution LED display. The expansion was driven by overwhelming demand: Billboard's reporting noted around three million people went online to buy tickets for the original dates. An artist presale for the January 2028 shows began on November 19, with general sale opening on November 20. The residency, promoted by Live Nation, marks P!NK's first Las Vegas residency and comes as Sphere has become one of the city's biggest live-entertainment draws. Concert and hotel packages are available through Vibee, including stays at The Venetian, the resort connected directly to the venue.

articles.title: BTS win Artist of the Year for a record eighth time as MAMA Awards 2026 open in Osaka
